articles.title: Kanye West questions what Lewis Hamilton sees in Kim Kardashian as their romance draws scrutiny
articles.summary: International Sports News: Kanye West has sparked fresh attention around Kim Kardashian’s reported romance with Lewis Hamilton after sharing his blunt opinion about the Formula .
articles.body: Kanye West has sparked fresh attention around Kim Kardashian’s reported romance with Lewis Hamilton after sharing his blunt opinion about the Formula 1 champion’s relationship with his former wife. West questioned Hamilton’s decision to date Kardashian, pointing to her four children and his own experience of their marriage. His remarks have added another layer of intrigue to a relationship that has attracted intense public interest throughout 2026.Kanye West shares blunt view on Lewis Hamilton and Kim KardashianWest did not hold back when asked about Hamilton and Kardashian. His comments focused less on the Formula 1 star’s fame and more on the realities of entering a relationship with someone who already has a family.“Honestly, I don’t understand how some guys think. I wish Lewis had someone who could give him some good advice, but apparently, he doesn’t. I just can’t understand how, at his age and with everything he’s accomplished, he’d choose to date a woman who already has four children with another man and be completely comfortable with that.“I’ve already experienced that relationship and everything that came with it, and to be honest, it’s nothing special, which makes me wonder what he sees in it. But he seems completely comfortable with the situation, and I guess that’s what matters to him. Personally, though, it’s not something I would ever choose for myself again.”The comments carry added weight because West and Kardashian were married for almost seven years. Kardashian filed for divorce in February 2021, and their divorce was finalised in November 2022. They share four children, with their settlement including joint custody and arrangements for shared expenses.West’s perspective also comes from having lived through the pressures that come with being part of the Kardashian family. His comments therefore offer a deeply personal view, although Hamilton’s reported relationship with Kardashian remains his own.Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton’s reported romance draws attentionHamilton and Kardashian have known each other for years. Their paths first crossed around 2014, when they attended the GQ Men of the Year Awards in London with their respective partners at the time.Their friendship continued as they moved through overlapping worlds of sport, fashion and entertainment. However, speculation about a possible romance intensified in 2026 after they were reportedly seen together during the New Year period in Aspen.Further appearances fueled the conversation. The pair were linked to trips and public outings, including time in Paris and at major entertainment and sporting events. Hamilton also appeared in content connected to Kardashian, while Kardashian was later seen supporting him at the Monaco Grand Prix.Their connection became even more closely watched after Hamilton reportedly spent part of the Fourth of July holiday with Kardashian and her family in Idaho. Reports also suggested that he had developed a comfortable relationship with her children.For now, the reported romance continues to command attention because of the people involved. Hamilton is one of Formula 1’s most accomplished stars, while Kardashian remains a major figure in entertainment and business. West’s latest comments have simply pushed their already high-profile relationship back into the spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Amid 'very long meetings' and running chess world, has Viswanathan Anand lost 'hunger' to win? | Exclusive
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: The English vocabulary sometimes feels the loss for words while describing what Viswanathan Anand is to India and its chess legacy. There i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The English vocabulary sometimes feels the loss for words while describing what Viswanathan Anand is to India and its chess legacy. There is a particular kind of stillness that follows the Chennai-born Grandmaster into a room, the stillness of a man who solved most of what chess could throw at him decades ago and has nothing left to prove to anyone in it.For over a month now, that stillness has been sitting in a very different chair. On July 24, 2026, Anand became interim President of FIDE, world chess's governing body, after Arkady Dvorkovich voluntarily stepped back from his duties under European Union and Swiss sanctions. The role is temporary by design as Anand's term runs out with the FIDE presidential elections on September 26.But for the two months he holds it, the man who has spent a lifetime being chess's most recognisable player is also, quite literally, running the sport."Fairly, (it's) kind of what I expected," the 56-year-old tells TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction, with that familiar half-smile doing most of the talking before the next sentences catch up."It's more work than being deputy president. When I was the deputy, I only had to step in when Arkady (Dvorkovich) couldn't make it. Now, in fact, I have to conduct a lot of the federation. But I've been doing it out of India mostly."The extra weight of countless responsibilities hasn't meant more miles, though."Actually, I've travelled less, but because I had already made plans like this. I've been attending many, many more meetings, quite often, very long Zoom meetings with lots of people from all over the world to discuss FIDE matters," added the former five-time world champion.The intensity, he says, has already peaked and passed."There was a period last week when that all peaked," he revealed. "Now everything, the agenda, is set for the General Assembly in Samarkand at the end of the year. For the last few days, it's been a bit lighter."And with that, amid the Zoom calls and federation business, the game of 64 squares has called in a more familiar manner.Anand returns to the Global Chess League (GCL) this year with Alaskan Knights. None of that administrative weight, it turns out, has dulled his appetite for the board."I can tell you my hunger for the GCL trophy is still there. I would very much love for us, though I'm playing with Alaskan Knights this year, to pull that off. I'm very motivated, and I hope to do my best and get us into the final first," the Grandmaster, who was one of the most prominent faces of Ganges Grandmasters for the last three seasons, remarked."It doesn't matter what you did in your career. If you're playing this tournament, then you enjoy it, and you try to play. The GCL is not the kind of event, typical event, that I used to play in. It is really a new kind of experience. For those 10 days to two weeks, I really enjoy myself."It may be a new team this year, but the fundamentals have not changed for Anand. "Many players in the GCL have already changed teams a couple of times. I think once I go there and meet my teammates, on the first day itself, it'll feel normal. I have played with Arjun before; two years ago, he was my teammate. There are familiar faces, and you'll just adjust," he remarked.Generally, I stick to my routine, that's all. It's not like I will keep a lot of FIDE meetingsBalancing a federation's crisis, family matters, and then chess, on paper, may look like a nightmare. But ask Anand, and then see the stillness follow."Generally, I stick to my routine, that's all. It's not like I will keep a lot of FIDE meetings; if there's some FIDE emergency, I might take a decision quickly, but otherwise I don't expect to have long meetings while I'm there. I focus very much on the GCL," he told this website, adding that he doesn't plan days in advance so much as meet them as they come."I know that I have to play against somebody tomorrow and I will get ready for it."Within weeks, the presidency will pass to someone else. Until then, world chess is being run by a man who, when the meetings end, still just wants to play. And according to Anand, the play, on offer between September 5-13 in Bengaluru, will be as competitive as "anywhere else".ALSO READ: 'Praggnanandhaa is No. 1 in the world': Viswanathan Anand after India's first Grand Chess Tour title"Of course, they are (competitive). Because of the kind of openings they play, you could think, 'Oh, they're not taking it seriously.' But in fact, they're simply adapting their approach for the faster time control, for the pressure of watching your teammates and making decisions based on the match situation," he concluded. "Once you take into account the different atmosphere, they are just as competitive as they are anywhere else."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asian Games: Another dope case clouds India's preparations
articles.summary: More sports News: New Delhi: Another positive dope test has hit India's preparations for the upcoming Asian Games, with wushu medal hopeful Surya Bhanupratap Singh beco.
articles.body: New Delhi: Another positive dope test has hit India's preparations for the upcoming Asian Games, with wushu medal hopeful Surya Bhanupratap Singh becoming the latest athlete to be provisionally suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).The 30-year-old from Jammu & Kashmir, a 2018 Jakarta Asian Games bronze medallist in the men's 60kg Sanda, failed an anti-doping test for Enobosarm (Ostarine), a selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) designed for muscle and bone development. Ostarine is strictly prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and classified under S1.2, or "other anabolic agents".Bhanupratap has been dropped from the Asian Games squad and his name deleted from the govt-approved final contingent.Bhanupratap's case takes the number of Indian athletes failing dope tests since the recent Glasgow Commonwealth Games to 12, an alarming spurt that has affected multiple disciplines and, in some cases, cost India competition quotas.The list comprises weightlifters N Ajith (71kg), Sairaj Pardeshi (88kg), Harcharan Singh (110kg) and Vanshita Verma (77kg); judokas Arun Kumar (73kg) and Tulika Maan (+78kg); shooter Gaurav Kumar Masoori (10m air pistol); rower Lakshya (lightweight double scull); wrestlers Mukul Dahiya (86kg freestyle) and Deepanshu (130kg Greco-Roman); runner Abhishek Pal (5,000m and 10,000m) and now Bhanupratap (65kg Sanda).The spurt in doping cases has already forced India to trim its weightlifting representation for the Asian Games. The Glasgow quota was hit by multiple violations, while only five lifters have been named for the Aichi-Nagoya multisport event - Mirabai Chanu (49kg), Gyaneshwari Yadav (53kg), Seram Nirupama Devi (61kg), Harjinder Kaur (69kg) and Rishikanta Singh (60kg).Wrestling has also lost two Asian Games spots, shrinking from 18 to 16 after Dahiya and Deepanshu were suspended.Bhanupratap was a strong medal prospect in the men's 65kg Sanda event. He is also a two-time World Wushu Championships bronze medallist, finishing third in the 60kg category in Jakarta in 2015 and Kazan in 2017. His 2018 Asian Games bronze came in the same category.With Bhanupratap's exclusion, India's wushu squad now comprises seven athletes. The latest case underlines the growing challenge for NADA and Indian sports authorities as they try to keep doping cheats out of Games squads.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Totti believes in Roma: “They can fight to the end.”
articles.summary: Francesco Totti is keeping an eye on Roma and, without giving too much away, isn’t ruling them out of the Scudetto race. The former Giallorossi captain is cu...
articles.body:
Francesco Totti is keeping an eye on Roma and, without giving too much away, isn't ruling them out of the Scudetto race.

The former Giallorossi captain is currently in Florence, where tomorrow, Wednesday, September 2nd, he will participate in the match between Fiorentina All Stars and Operazione Nostalgia Legends at the Franchi stadium, organized to mark the Viola's centenary celebrations.

Speaking to Sky Sport , Totti discussed the start of Gian Piero Gasperini's team and its chances of staying close to the big teams until the end: "As a fan, I can't say, but they've started off on the right foot."

"We're just getting started; the transfer window has closed, and now the real championship begins. I hope Roma can have a great run with Inter, Napoli, and Juve; these are the teams I believe can fight until the end. Given the way they've started, there's a chance, but we're not saying anything."

articles.body:
The Boys from Vila, in the U-17 category, came from behind to beat Botafogo 4-2 on the afternoon of Tuesday (1) at CT Rei Pelé! Nadson scored twice, while Ignácio Salmon and João Borges added the other goals in Santos' great victory.

After falling behind 1-0 in the opening minutes, Peixe responded in the first half and turned it around to 2-1. Nadson equalized with an individual play down the right, and the comeback came from the left after João Borges set up Nadson inside the box.

In the second half, Santos were pegged back, but striker Ignácio, shortly after coming on, restored the lead with a cross-shot. Then, in stoppage time, João Borges fired high from inside the box to seal the final score.

With the win, the Boys from Vila remain in the race to qualify for the second phase. They are in 9th place, with 20 points from 14 matches.

On Saturday (5), they return to the field for the 15th round of the Brazilian Championship, against São Paulo at CT Marcelo Portugal, in Cotia, at 3:00 pm.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Doesn’t Hold Back on Working With Chargers OC, Mike McDaniel
articles.summary: Jim Harbaugh, during an appearance on the "Rich Eisen Show", gave a detailed description of what it's like working with Chargers offensive coordinator, Mike...
articles.body:
Jim Harbaugh has never been afraid to speak his mind. He, and the Harbaugh's generally ooze positivity, no matter the topic. He's long been a fan of his Los Angeles Chargers, starting-quarterback, Justin Herbert. And now, he has a new "toy" at his disposal.

Enter newly hired, Chargers offensive coordinator, Mike McDaniel. Near the start of the 2026 calendar, McDaniel added this new title to his resume. McDaniel was fired as the head coach of the Miami Dolphins on January 8 but didn't spend much time on the unemployment list.

Just 18 days later, on January 26, McDaniel was officially signing on the dotted-lien to become a member of the Chargers organization. Since then, he's been in charge of the team's offense. One of the benefits of taking the job is certainly being afforded the opportunity to coach Herbert.

Jim Harbaugh Provides Detailed Description of Mike McDaniel

But now, it's McDaniel who's being viewed as the uber-talented addition to the organization. And this week, during an appearance on the "Rich Eisen Show" on ESPN, Harbaugh was asked what it's like working with McDaniel. Harbaugh, as always, peeled back the curtain in only the way he can.

"He's so intelligent. Book smart, football smart, all the smarts, street smarts, uh, you name it," Harbaugh said.

Ahead of the upcoming 2026-27 NFL season, Harbaugh and McDaniel appear to be full of pure positivity. And a lot of that is surrounded by the opportunity to coach their starting QB, (Justin) Herbert.

Well, Harbaugh, the coach who produced a National Champion at the University of Michigan at the College level, and brought the San Francisco 49ers to a Super Bowl appearance, appears to defer to the likes of McDaniel and Herbert — at least in terms of intelligence.

"The kind of mirror reflection of that (McDaniel), is Justin Herbert. The intelligence and the football intelligence. It's such a great thing. People ask me, 'Well, how smart are they, coach?' I don't know. They're so smart, I don't know how smart they are. But, I know one thing, it bodes really well for the Los Angeles Chargers," Harbaugh said.

"He's just a great guy. He's hilarious, he's funny. The meetings that he has, I've got my pen out, I'm writing things down, because there's like a nugget of gold that comes out of every one of those interactions. Whether him and I are talking on the field, or in his office, or mine, or in the meetings. He just does it in a way that man, I like to listen to this guy talk. This man sure can talk, and I like what he's saying, and he's got the keys to the offense, and we're all behind him," Harbaugh said.

McDaniel Reveals Moment He Wanted to Work For Chargers

While Harbaugh has nothing but nice things to say about McDaniel after working with him for a few months, McDaniel recently revealed the moment he knew he wanted to work alongside Harbaugh .

And ultimately, over breakfast, McDaniel realized Los Angeles, coaching alongside (Jim) Harbaugh, coaching a (Justin) Herbert led offense, was the next step he needed to take in his career.

"In the morning, I met with Jim (Harbaugh) and John Spanos, and it was in that breakfast, through conversation I was like, let me call Cleveland real quick. I need to cancel some of the stuff I have upcoming because this is definitely the place I need to be," McDaniel said.

articles.title: Former NDSU Coach a Contender For Power 4 Job Analyst Says
articles.summary: Former North Dakota State Bison head coach and current Fresno State Bulldogs head coach Matt Entz is a contender for a Power Four job in 2027. The post Forme...
articles.body:
Before Tim Polasek led North Dakota State to the FBS, former Bison head coach Matt Entz had the move on his radar.

Entz left NDSU after the 2023 season to coach linebackers at USC before he took the head coaching job with Fresno State in 2025. With Entz's success between the Bison and Bulldogs, ESPN's Adam Rittenberg identified him as a prime candidate for a Power Four program next year.

"Entz has championships in his profile, leading North Dakota State to FCS titles in 2019 and 2021, and he went 60-11 there, with four top-three finishes in five years," Rittenberg wrote. "He then made the somewhat surprising move to USC, where he spent the 2024 season as a defensive assistant, gaining Power 4 experience, before taking the Fresno State job and going 9-4. Another strong season at Fresno State would put the 53-year-old on the radar for jobs spanning from the Midwest to the West Coast."

An Iowa native, Entz joined the Bison coaching staff in 2014 under former head coach Chris Klieman. Entz served as the defensive coordinator and linebackers coach from 2014 to 2018 before he took the head coaching job after Klieman left for Kansas State.

During Entz' time in Fargo, FBS talk had been simmering, though geography and budget had been main obstacles, and it never came to fruition under his watch despite attempts in 2020 with the shuffling of college football due to COVID-19.

Matt Entz Coaching Against His Former Team

Entz will coach against USC to open the season on Friday at the LA Coliseum, and he sees it as an early opportunity for his team to push for a College Football Playoff spot.

The Bulldogs joined the Pac-12 this year as one of five teams that left the Mountain West Conference , which made way for NDSU, Northern Illinois and UTEP . Entz believes his core of 14-15 starters are key to his team's chances for a run.

"Notre Dame and Oregon tout 15 returning starters; Georgia and USC also are among Power conference teams fielding some of the sport's most experienced rosters with at least 14 returners," Entz said via USA Today's Trojans Wire . "There's the potential for more for Fresno."

"I think our players are seeing that 'Hey, this experience is bigger than just me. I can get wherever I want from Fresno State," Entz added. "Now, at the same time, we have another successful season, it's going to get harder and harder to retain some of these players because, again, there are lucrative opportunities out there."

Fresno State will have plenty of challenges ahead beyond USC in hopes of making a run for the CFP. The Pac-12 notably had contenders in Boise State and San Diego State to tangle with.

When Entz took the job with USC in 2024, he spoke highly of his time with the Bison. Entz served on USC head coach Lincoln Riley's staff for one season when the Trojans went 7-6.

"I loved my time at NDSU," Entz told reporters in 2024. "It was an unbelievable 10 years. Had an opportunity to compete for seven national championships."

"That fan base there has an unbelievable standard and that's what makes that place so great," Entz added. "It's not about being 7-5. It's about winning championships. It's about winning national championships — and doing it with the right people, the right way. And I think this place can be the exact same thing."

articles.title: ‘Grow up…’ Ben Johnson explains how Chicago Bears helped take out Caleb Williams’ ‘goofy’ side
articles.summary: Caleb Williams has adopted a more serious approach since his time with the Chicago Bears, and Ben Johnson explained how the youngster’s maturity has come abo...
articles.body:
Caleb Williams has adopted a more serious approach since his time with the Chicago Bears, and Ben Johnson explained how the youngster's maturity has come about.

Williams has been on the receiving end of criticism from some fans for his demeanour and general attitude off the field, with people taking umbrage at his aloof disposition.

However, heading into the 2026 season, Johnson and the Bears coaching staff are thrilled to see a far more focused approach.

Why Caleb Williams 'goofy' demeanour is no longer a problem for Ben Johnson

Speaking to reporters ahead of the Chicago Bears' Gameweek 1 fixture against the Carolina Panthers, HC Ben Johnson was asked about the difference he's seen in Caleb Williams this season.

He admitted that Williams abandoned his 'goofy' and aloof approach for a more intentional and serious one this season, and he is growing into a leadership role.

"I've seen a very composed person every time he steps into the building. This guy might have had a little goofy to him a year ago, and I use that term with love.

"Now you see a more serious player and intent every time around him. I think his teammates feel that as well.

"He's getting to the practice field early, he's making sure his part is taken care of, he's warmed up and ready to go, he's staying with the guys after practice. You see that on a regular basis.

"He's taken a lot of pride in his approach right now, and it trickles down to everyone around him. I think it is a great thing. I think he continues to grow up, and he's going to be a huge leader for us this year."

Williams had an excellent season last year, and was even getting MVP consideration for the way he helped the Bears go from a perennially losing team to a genuine Super Bowl contender.

While the youngster couldn't overcome league MVP Matthew Stafford and the Rams in the playoffs, his performance last season has given the Bears an excellent foundation to build on.

articles.title: Reaparece el Ferrari de Michael Jordan en el que Nike se inspiró para diseñar sus zapatillas
articles.standfirst: El Ferrari 550 Maranello de Michael Jordan, el mismo en el que se inspiró el diseño de las Air Jordan XIV, vuelve a salir a la luz después de más de dos décadas en paradero desconocido.
articles.summary: El Ferrari 550 Maranello de Michael Jordan, el mismo en el que se inspiró el diseño de las Air Jordan XIV, vuelve a salir a la luz después de más de dos décadas en paradero desconocido.
articles.body: El 13 de junio de 1997, Michael Jordan acababa de conquistar su quinto campeonato de la NBA. Horas después de levantar el trofeo en el United Center, cogió el Ferrari 550 Maranello que ves en estas imágenes y se marchó a su casa mientras se iba fumando un puro. El coche resultaba ya entonces inolvidable: pintura Rosso Barchetta, llantas Speedline cromadas (no son las de serie), interior de cuero tostado... y por si había dudas, una matrícula de Illinois con las letras MJ 5. Ver a Jordan por aquellos años con ese Ferrari era normal, pese a que no parecía el coche más apropiado con sus 1,98 metros de estatura. De hecho, Ferrari tuvo que adaptar el puesto de conducción a la envergadura del jugador, de forma que el asiento vino con raíles en el suelo más largos y un acolchado más fino para que pudiera retrasar todo lo posible su posición de conducción. Al coche le correspondió el chasis 108712 y fue entregado a Jordan el 29 de mayo de 1997 a través de Foreign Cars Italia, en Greensboro, Carolina del Norte. La tarjeta de garantía original sigue junto al coche y conserva la firma del propio jugador, además de su dirección de Durham. Bajo el largo capó rojo latía un motor V12 de 5,5 litros (identificado como Tipo F133A) que entregaba 485 CV y se asociaba a una caja de cambios manual de 6 velocidades. Gracias a él, el Maranello era capaz de alcanzar 320 km/h con una banda sonora mecánica que hoy pertenece a otra era. Entre 1996 y 2001 se fabricaron 3.083 unidades. No es por tanto un edición limitada o súper exclusiva, pero la tirada fue suficientemente corta como para que nos acordemos del día que vimos uno, si es que hemos tenido esa oportunidad. Pero el de Jordan era especial no solo por su asiento adaptado y su pertenencia, porque aquí es cuando Nike entra en juego. Cuando un diseñador llamado Tinker Hatfield trabajaba en el diseño de las Air Jordan XIV, tuvo de repente una referencia que se empeñó en seguir: el mítico Ferrari del jugador estrella. El cuero acolchado evocaba el habitáculo del Maranello, las formas de la carrocería encontraron su reflejo en los volúmenes de la zapatilla, las rejillas de ventilación inspiraron algunos de sus detalles y el dibujo de la suela tomó referencias del neumático. Hasta el famoso emblema encontró su correspondencia, ya que el Jumpman quedó integrado en un escudo que recordaba al del Cavallino Rampante. Ferrari y Jordan terminaron compartiendo lenguaje de diseño en un objeto que se llevaba puesto. Esta conexión fue agraciada con su momento de gloria el 14 de junio de 1998, durante el sexto partido de las Finales de la NBA frente a Utah Jazz. Jordan estrenó las Air Jordan XIV y, a falta de 5,2 segundos, lanzó el tiro en suspensión sobre Bryon Russell que dio el campeonato a Chicago. Fue el célebre Last Shot. La última canasta de Jordan como jugador de los Bulls. Y el sexto anillo de su carrera. Durante sus últimos años en Chicago, Jordan utilizó aquel Ferrari para acudir a partidos, entrenamientos y otras apariciones públicas. El coche sumó unos 10.300 kilómetros, pero Jordan lo vendió el 4 de diciembre de 2002 a través de Lake Forest Sportscars, en Illinois. A partir de ahí, el coche desapareció del radar público. Durante casi 24 años, el Ferrari en concreto que había inspirado a unas zapatillas legendarias quedó fuera del circuito habitual de los coleccionistas, hasta convertirse en una de esas piezas de las que se habla mucho pero nadie ve. Todo aquel anonimato en el que había caído el coche acabó cuando John Temerian, cofundador de Curated (venden y restauran coches deportivos y de lujo en Miami), encontró con una pista decisiva en un foro de internet después de 10 años buscando aquel coche. Allí apareció el número de chasis, que según los registros de Ferrari seguía vinculado a Michael Jordan y la matrícula MJ 5. La investigación permitió al final descubrir que el coche estaba en California, donde llevaba años en manos del mismo propietario y permanecía fuera del mercado. Temerian terminó comprándolo sin haberlo visto en persona, así que el 29 de mayo de 2026, justo 29 años después de que Ferrari entregara el coche a Jordan, el Maranello regresó a Chicago. Pero Temerian no buscó y encontró el coche por hobby, sino como negocio, y después de ponerlo al día desde un punto de vista estético y mecánico lo va a subastar el próximo 15 de septiembre a través de Joopiter. El Ferrari luce su pintura Rosso Barchetta, las mismas llantas Speedline cromadas, el interior de cuero tostado, la matrícula histórica MJ 5 y sus aproximadamente 10.300 kilómetros. Pero, sobre todo, conserva una conexión extraordinaria entre tres mundos que rara vez coinciden en un mismo objeto, Ferrari, Michael Jordan y las Air Jordan XIV. Y es por eso que, cuando un 550 Maranello 'normal' con tan pocos kilómetros se puede encontrar por unos 200.000 euros, el de Jordan se espera que se venda por entre 600.000 y 1.100.000 euros.

articles.title: Egoitz Bijueska, en MARCA: "Hubo momentos en los que pensé en dejarlo"
articles.standfirst: El skater español afronta el final de una temporada que ya es histórica... con el sueño olímpico cada vez más presente
articles.summary: El skater español afronta el final de una temporada que ya es histórica... con el sueño olímpico cada vez más presente
articles.body: Egoitz Bijueska es el mejor en lo suyo. Lleva un tiempo siéndolo. No debe ser sencillo con apenas 15 años. Ha ganado Copas del Mundo, ha hecho historia en los X Games logrando la victoria por delante del oro y la plata olímpicas. Toca sumar, a este expediente brillante, la imposibilidad de brillar en su país. Una nueva fuga de talento rumbo a EEUU, está vez en skate, que aprovecha unos días en la península para visitar MARCA y charlar sobre su pasado, su presente y su futuro... en el que las olimpiadas cada vez tienen más peso. PREGUNTA: Leí que a los siete años era el peor de sus amigos en skate, ¿cómo es posible? RESPUESTA: Es cierto, en esa época solía ser el el peor en las clases de skate, pero seguí entrenando más que todos ellos. P.: ¿Cómo ha sido esa evolución hasta llegar al lugar en el que está hoy? R.: Ha sido difícil, los primeros años era más un juego, hasta los 9 o 10 años. Luego empecé a participar en campeonatos de Euskadi, campeonatos a nivel nacional y fui escalando hasta llegar a campeonatos del mundo a los 12 años y de ahí ya empecé a mejorar a nivel internacional. P.: ¿Cuál es la mayor dificultad que ha encontrado en este proceso? R.: Sobre todo gente que te deja de lado, o momentos en los que no tienes ganas de entrenar y tienes que ir. También compañeros que lo van dejando, que solías practicar con ellos y al final lo dejan. P.: Hace un tiempo, después de tu primera Copa del Mundo, me dijo que no sentía miedo cuando ejecutabas sus trucos, ¿sigue sin tener miedo? R.: Depende el momento. Hay momentos en los que te da miedo, tienes la inseguridad de si lo vas a hacer bien o mal en las competiciones, de algunos trucos o maniobras que son muy difíciles y te da miedo. P.: Ahora pasa gran parte del año en EEUU, ¿cómo es su vida allí? R.: Por las mañanas entreno, normalmente lo hago por la mañana y por la tarde, entre medias estudio y luego ya a última hora de la tarde tengo tiempo para ir con mis amigos a la playa o a surfear. P.: ¿Qué es lo mejor de vivir allí? R.: Sobre todo las instalaciones que tienes para entrenar. Siempre hay gente para entrenar, porque aquí en España suelo estar solo. P.: A nivel de skateparks, ¿cuál es la gran diferencia con España? R.: Aparte del volumen de instalaciones, que en Estados Unidos siempre hay más, también la altura y cómo están hechos y fabricados los skateparks, pero sobre todo la altura. P.: Porque para quién no lo sepa, en España no hay un solo skatepark que este al nivel de las condiciones a las que luego se enfrenta en las competiciones internacionales. Es como si Alonso entrena con un coche de calle entre semana y el domingo se sube a un F1, ¿me equivoco? R.: Eso es (sonríe). P.: Lleva una temporada tremendamente exitosa, ¿qué victoria le ha hecho más ilusión? R.: Te diría que el campeonato de Brasil que gané en marzo. Otro campeonato del mundo. Fue una semana en la que recibí muchos golpes, fue muy difícil y encima me lo jugué todo en la última ronda. P.: ¿Y cómo valora su paso por los X-Games? R.: Al final fueron tres campeonatos y los tres me salieron bien. Fue un campeonato bastante divertido, me lo pasé muy bien. P.: ¿Cómo es conocer a sus ídolos en el mundo del skate? R.: Es increíble conocer a los ídolos que he tenido de pequeño y estar compitiendo contra ellos y pensar venga ahora te gano yo, luego me ganas tú. Es un subidón. P.: ¿Cuál es el mejor consejo que ha recibido en esta aventura rodeado de sus referentes? R.: Yo creo que el no dejarlo, porque ha habido momentos que te planteas dejarlo. Luego siempre vienen tiempos mejores y al final te lo acabas pasando bien. Ahora tengo amigos y me está yendo bien en el skate. P.: ¿Cuándo se lo planteó? R.: Cuando tenía como 11, 12 años que tenía que entrenar aquí siempre, no había nadie con el que entrenar, las instalaciones eran malas... pero sigues teniendo resultados buenos. Al final todos los días tienes que ir a entrenar solo y en sitios malos, pues te planteas dejarlo. P.: ¿Cómo se ve en el futuro? R.: Me veo siendo pro del skate en Estados Unidos, viviendo por allí. P.: ¿Y con qué sueña? R.: Ganar las olimpiadas. P.: ¿Cree que lo puede hacer? R.: Espero.

articles.title: Cricketers to get best rooms at Asian Games 2026, says Japanese official
articles.summary: Cricket is a minor sport in Japan, but it will provide the best accommodation to participating teams, the official says.
articles.body:
Cricketers at this month’s Asian Games in Japan will have better accommodation than athletes from many other sports, the head of Japanese cricket has said amid growing concerns about a lack of five-star hotels for players.

A Sri Lankan official said this week that some of Asia’s top teams had raised doubts over facilities and accommodation at the games, taking place in Nagoya and the wider Aichi area from September 19.

Cricket is a minor sport in Japan, and its fixtures will be played at a new purpose-built ground, with reports of tents serving as dressing rooms and distant toilet facilities.

There is no dedicated athletes’ village at the games, with organisers instead relying on cabins in a cruise ship, rooms in temporary wooden containers and hotels.

Organisers said last week that accommodation was already stretched to the limit after the number of Asian Games athletes ballooned to 17,000.

The number of athletes in the 2024 Paris Olympics was about 11,000.

The cricket tournament is being run by the Asian Games organising committee in collaboration with the Asian Cricket Council (ACC).

Japan Cricket Association CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji said the two bodies had been discussing accommodation options “for a long time”.

“The participating teams in cricket are being offered hotel accommodation,” Miyaji said on Wednesday.

“Many other sports are being accommodated in much more limited facilities, such as a cruise ship or container hotels.”

Matches will be played at Korogi Sports Park, a converted baseball field that is a 40-minute train ride from central Nagoya.

Media reports in India said the country’s cricket board was unhappy with arrangements and might send a second-string squad after originally naming 15 players led by Shreyas Iyer and including 15-year-old rising star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.

Miyaji said the organisers “only had 17 months to prepare and had to start from scratch” for cricket at the games.

He said they had been working “to ensure that the best facilities are provided within the limited timeline and facility restrictions”.

“Despite being temporary, the facilities will provide as comfortable a space as possible for the players and officials,” he said.

Miyaji said the pitch, which is being prepared by the curator of the 35,000-capacity Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Sri Lanka, would be of a high standard.

“From what I have seen, the playing surface and field will be the best seen in cricket’s inclusion in the Asian Games,” he added.

articles.title: "¿Para qué va a pedir perdón Julián? ¿Quién le va a creer?"
articles.standfirst: Jorge Segura analiza en La Tribu la situación del delantero del Atlético de Madrid tras su fichaje frustrado por el Barcelona
articles.summary: Jorge Segura analiza en La Tribu la situación del delantero del Atlético de Madrid tras su fichaje frustrado por el Barcelona
articles.body: Jorge Segura, Diego Picó, Nacho Palencia, Ricardo Sierra, Nacho Labarga y Ramón Álvarez de Mon han sido los tertulianos de este miércoles en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar el cierre del mercado de fichajes, la situación de Julián Álvarez y el regreso de Mourinho. Jorge Segura. "Julián no me parece para tanto. No me parece que haya sido decisivo ni en el City ni en el Atlético. Pedir perdón... ¿para qué?, ¿quién le va a creer? Independientemente de que se haya equivocado, se le ve afectado anímicamente". Diego Picó. "Estoy convencido de que el 1 de enero habrá second round con el caso Julián, pero ahora tienes que rehabilitarlo. Son cuatro meses en los que necesitas que el futblista te ayude. Simeone ya ha empezado a lanzar mensajes. Julián tiene que pedir perdón por las formas". Nacho Palencia. "Es muy posible que, de aquí a enero, Julián no siga con su representante actual, que ha sido el que le ha metido en este laberinto. La gente tiene que entender que el Atleti necesita a Julián para pelear los objetivos, y que si Julián habló fue casi medio obligado por su entorno y por el Barça. Le han ido metiendo en un callejón sin salida, y ese callejón se llama Hidalgo y Barcelona. Seguir pitando a Julián perjudica a Koke, a Barrios, a Oblak, a Simeone... Hay que hacer un reseat". Ricardo Sierra. "Puede estar mal asesorado, pero tiene su parte de responsabilidad. Julián no se va a volver a ganar el cariño de los aficionados, pero al menos que se gane el respeto. Si sale ahora a pedir perdón, mucha gente no le va a creer. Lo que tiene que hacer es trabajar, el Atleti y sus compañeros arroparle y el público tiene que pensar que es un activo del club y, aunque no le quiera, respetarle si él se lo gana con su profesionalidad y con goles". Nacho Labarga. "Lo que tiene que hacer Julián es marcar goles y, cuando lo haga, pedir perdón, deslizar que se ha sentido engañado, que ha gestionado mal la situación y tirar hacia delante. Me parece muy complicado. Yo hubiese apostado por una cesión a última hora porque el Atleti tiene un problema, Julián tiene un problema y el Cholo tiene un problema". Ramón Álvarez de Mon. "La afición del Atlético convivió con un Griezmann que hizo 'La Decisión', que se quedó finalmente pero públicamente dudó, y convivió con un Griezmann que volvió después de no triunfar en el Barcelona".

articles.title: ¿Por qué la multa a Raúl Asencio es de 14.400 euros y qué tendrá que hacer para recuperar el carné?
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Real Madrid tendrá que seguir un procedimiento y esperar ocho meses antes de poder volver a ponerse al volante de cualquier vehículo.
articles.summary: El defensa del Real Madrid tendrá que seguir un procedimiento y esperar ocho meses antes de poder volver a ponerse al volante de cualquier vehículo.
articles.body: La condena por un delito contra la seguridad vial que le ha caído a Raúl Asencio no se limita a la multa de 14.400 euros y a la retirada del carné durante ocho meses. Además del daño para su imagen, el futbolista tendrá que cumplir una serie de trámites y plazos marcados por la ley antes de poder volver a sentarse al volante. Sí. El artículo 73 de la Ley sobre Tráfico, Circulación de Vehículos a Motor y Seguridad Vial obliga a cualquier conductor al que se le haya quitado el carné de conducir por sentencia firme a superar un curso de sensibilización y reeducación vial antes de poder recuperarlo. En el caso de Asencio, al tratarse de una condena igual o inferior a dos años, bastará con que demuestre que ha superado con aprovechamiento ese curso, sin necesidad de pasar de nuevo el examen teórico en la DGT que sí se exige a quienes pierden el permiso por sentencias superiores a dos años o por agotamiento de puntos. El curso es de 20 horas de duración y se imparte en centros autorizados por la DGT, y Asencio podría empezar a hacerlo ya mismo, aunque solo recuperará el permiso una vez que hayan pasado esos ocho meses. En cuanto al precio, su coste ronda entre los 300 y los 450 euros en función de la comunidad autónoma y el centro elegido. Aquí entran en juego dos escenarios distintos. Si durante estos ocho meses de retirada del carné Asencio condujera cualquier vehículo no cometería una simple infracción administrativa, sino un nuevo delito, tipificado en el artículo 384 del Código Penal, castigado con prisión de tres a seis meses, multa de doce a veinticuatro meses o trabajos en beneficio de la comunidad, además de que el tiempo sin poder conducir legalmente se ampliaría. Si, en cambio, una vez recuperado el carné volviera a ser sorprendido conduciendo bajo los efectos del alcohol, entraría en juego la agravante de reincidencia del artículo 22.8 del Código Penal, que endurece la pena para quien ya cuenta con una condena firme por un delito similar. En la práctica, esto significa que a Asencio le podrían caer un máximo de seis meses de prisión, doce meses de multa o cuatro años sin carné. No existe una cuota fija para este tipo de multas. En una multa penal, es el juez quien fija tanto el número de días de condena, en función de la gravedad de los hechos como el importe de cada cuota. Esta cuota se establece en teoría teniendo en cuenta la situación económica del condenado, valorando su patrimonio, sus ingresos y sus cargas familiares, lo que no quita que la cifra de 120 euros parezca muy baja para un futbolista de élite como él En cualquier caso, es cierto que la ley marca que esta cuota oscile entre 2 y 400 euros diarios, y el tribunal está obligado a motivar por qué fija una cifra concreta. Los 120 euros diarios impuestos a Asencio están lejos del máximo legal, aunque por lo visto se sitúan muy por encima de lo habitual para un ciudadano medio. Con todo, las cifras de condena y multa quedan por debajo de lo que marca la ley para este tipo de delito. Esto se debe al parecer a que Asencio reconoció los hechos y aceptó la pena propuesta por la Fiscalía en el juicio rápido celebrado en San Bartolomé de Tirajana. Y según la ley de Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal, cuando el acusado acepta los hechos ante el juzgado de guardia la pena solicitada se reduce en un tercio. Aplicado sobre los mínimos legales, seis meses de multa se convierten en cuatro y doce meses de retirada de carné se quedan en ocho, exactamente las cifras que recoge la sentencia.

articles.title: Stan Kroenke, el amo del deporte USA, llega también a la MLB con Los Angeles Angels
articles.standfirst: El dueño de los Nuggets (NBA), Los Ángeles Rams (NFL) y los Colorado Avalanche (NHL), entre otros, completa su presencia en las grandes Ligas de Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El dueño de los Nuggets (NBA), Los Ángeles Rams (NFL) y los Colorado Avalanche (NHL), entre otros, completa su presencia en las grandes Ligas de Estados Unidos
articles.body: A Stan Kroenke sólo le faltaba un equipo en la Major League de Béisbol (MLB) para ser propietario de una franquicia en cada una de las grandes Ligas Profesionales de Estados Unidos. Estaba presente en la NBA con los Denver Nuggets, en la NFL con Los Ángeles Rams y en la NHL con los Colorado Avalanche. También en la MLS con los Colorado Rapids. Su radio de acción, a través de la empresa Kroenke Sports and Entertainment (KSE), se extiende también a la Premier con el Arsenal. Ahora ha llegado a un acuerdo para comprar Los Angeles Angels. La venta está prevista para hacerse oficial en el primer trimestre del 2027, pendiente de la aprobación de MLB. "Los Angels son una franquicia histórica arraigada en un gran mercado. Esperamos un futuro emocionante", comentó Stan Kroenke, de 79 años, en un comunicado. La operación se cerraría en un precio de unos 4.000 millones de dólares, según desvela ESPN. Supera el récord anterior de la venta de un equipo en la MLB cuando los San Diego Padres fueron adquiridos por 3.900 millones por parte de un grupo de inversores liderado por el empresario José E. Feliciano, a su vez uno de los dueños del Chelsea. Los Angels estaban en manos de Arte Moreno, primer propietario mayoritario latino de la MLB, desde que comprara el equipo a Disney en 2003, justo después de que el equipo ganara su primer y único título de las Series Mundiales. "Para la familia Moreno ha sido un honor estar al frente de los Angels durante 23 años y creemos que, gracias a la experiencia y el éxito de KSE, ellos son los mejores sucesores para la franquicia", dijo Moreno en un comunicado. Kroenke construyó buena parte de su patrimonio en el sector inmobiliario. Puso en pie centros comerciales cerca de las tiendas de las cadenas de grandes almacenes Walmart, en su día propiedad de su suegro y cuyas acciones luego pasaron a su mujer Ann Walton Kroenke y su cuñada. Su fortuna se estima en unos 24.000 millones de dólares. Kroenke compró los Colorado Avalanche en el año 2000 como parte de una operación de unos 450 millones de dólares, que también incluyó a los Denver Nuggets y al entonces Pepsi Center de Denver, hoy conocido como Ball Arena. En 2023 los Nuggets conquistaron el anillo de la NBA. Los Colorado Rapids ganaron la MLS Cup en 2010. También es dueño de un equipo de lacrosse, Colorado Mammoth, que ganó la Liga Nacional en 2006 y 2022. Mientras que los Colorado Avalanche levnataron la Stanley Cup en 2001 y 2022. Su historia en la NFL arrancó en 1995 cuando adquirió el 40 % de los Rams, por entonces con sede en Saint Louis. Ganó la SuperBowl en 2000, Tras la muerte de Georgia Frontiere en 2008, la otra propietaria del equipo que heredó al fallecimiento de su marido Carroll Rosenbloom, Kroenke compró el 60% restante. Ocho años después trasladó el equipo a Los Ángeles. Volvió a ganar la SuperBowll en 2022. Tomó el control del Arsenal en 2011 tras haber ostentado antes el 30 por ciento de su propiedad. Su hijo Josh Kroenke se puso al frente de la gestión como copropietario de un club que este año defiende su título de la Premier.

articles.title: NHL insider drops major Auston Matthews hint as Maple Leafs captain nears a potentially historic extension
articles.summary: NHL News: Auston Matthews enters the new Toronto Maple Leafs season with more than a return to form on the line. The captain has two years remaining on his $13..
articles.body: Auston Matthews enters the new Toronto Maple Leafs season with more than a return to form on the line. The captain has two years remaining on his $13.25 million contract, but his next deal could reset the NHL salary market. Leafs insider Michael Augello believes Matthews could eventually seek between $19 million and $20 million per season if the coming season goes well. With the salary cap climbing and several elite players landing massive extensions, Toronto may soon face a defining decision on the future of its franchise star.Could Auston Matthews land a $19 million to $20 million contract?Augello’s prediction is tied closely to what Auston Matthews does this season. The 29-year-old has not produced at his previous level over the past two seasons, making the upcoming campaign particularly important for both sides.“This season is the key,” he said while appearing on The Leafs Convo podcast. “They’re never going to allow him to get to UFA. But if he scores 40 goals this year and they make the playoffs and he says he wants to stay in Toronto, the organization clearly wants to keep him here. Then he’s probably going to be asking […] a contract with significant terms, probably seven years max, and it’s probably going to be $19-20 million. That’s the reality now.”That number would be enormous, but the league has already started moving in that direction.Leo Carlsson agreed to an offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers worth $18 million per season, which Anaheim matched. Macklin Celebrini then signed an extension carrying an $18.8 million cap hit from next season. Cale Makar went even higher, signing a deal with a $20.4 million annual cap hit.Matthews does not need to beat those figures to command a huge raise. If he returns to the scoring form that produced 69 goals in 2023-24, a contract around that range becomes much easier to justify.When can Auston Matthews sign his next Maple Leafs extension?Auston Matthews cannot sign his next extension until next summer, giving Toronto and the player another season to assess where things stand.The Maple Leafs missed the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season for the first time in a decade, while general manager John Chayka has made significant changes across the organization. The club hopes those moves can put it back into contention, but Matthews’ individual performance will remain one of the biggest factors.His health is also worth watching. Matthews suffered a Grade 3 MCL sprain after taking a knee-on-knee hit from then-Anaheim Ducks captain Radko Gudas in early March. The injury ended his season, while Gudas received a five-game suspension.Matthews is expected to be healthy for training camp later this month. That matters because Toronto needs to see the version of its captain that can drive an offense before committing to what could become the richest contract in franchise history.For now, the situation is fairly clear. articles.title: Why AEW is Winning the Pro Wrestling War vs. WWE in 2026
articles.summary: AEW presented the biggest show on its calendar, All In, from Wembley Stadium in London this past Sunday, an extravaganza that had everything fans crave from professional wrestling: surprises, the culmination of lengthy storylines, excellent in-ring content, and a new champion crowned in an extraordinary main event.
articles.body:
AEW presented the biggest show on its calendar, All In, from Wembley Stadium in London this past Sunday, an extravaganza that had everything fans crave from professional wrestling: surprises, the culmination of lengthy storylines, excellent in-ring content, and a new champion crowned in an extraordinary main event.

As that pay-per-view went off the air, it became abundantly clear that here in 2026, AEW is winning the pro wrestling war vs. WWE.

Sure, the latter is still backing up the Brinks trucks and making serious bank, but AEW has eclipsed the industry leader in several other categories to support that argument.

AEW's All In pay-per-view event culminated Sunday in London with Will Ospreay paying off his long journey to the top of the pro wrestling mountain by defeating Kenny Omega to win the company's world title.

Tony Khan and his creative team did not overthink the situation, book a shocking outcome for the sake of it, or worry themselves too much with whether the audience would sniff out the finish or not.

They produced the finish that everyone in Wembley Stadium wanted to see, with Ospreay capturing the title in his hometown, resulting in one of the most memorable and emotional moments in company history.

It is something AEW has done consistently in 2026, putting the appropriate exclamation point on storylines up and down the card. Look no further than Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight from the same show. Allin avenged Knight's betrayal, took him out in similar fashion to the attacks he suffered, and won the TNT title. A simple story, with a simple outcome, that fans ate up.

Even the Brawling Birds' Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor arriving to their home country and doing the seemingly impossible by knocking off Divine Dominion for the women's tag titles was the appropriate and satisfying conclusion to a that rivalry.

Dating back to last summer, WWE has adopted a creative strategy to try and stay ahead of the audience. It most famously had Seth Rollins feign a knee injury so it could surprise fans with a Money in the Bank cash-in at the conclusion of the 2025 SummerSlam event.

That works in the moment and creates buzz, but it is gimmicky and does not encourage long-term buy-in to the stories and rivalries that play out each week.

Then there is the potential for TKO interference, as we witnessed this past WrestleMania, with the shoehorning of Pat McAfee into a Cody Rhodes-Randy Orton story that did not need him.

The potential that something of that nature can happen on a whim makes it very difficult for the company to provide the type of long-term storytelling and suitable payoff that it delivered at WrestleMania 40 in 2024, when Cody Rhodes finished his story.

For years, no matter the quality of either company's product, there was one consistent: WWE had the superior women's division. Thanks to the work of Charlotte Flair, Becky Lynch, Bayley, Rhea Ripley, Iyo Sky, and Bianca Belair, the company vastly outperformed AEW in that regard.

While WWE has the talent and the matches have been good-to-great when need be, the AEW women's division has not suffered from the injuries or questionable creative that WWE's has.

The result is an area of the roster that has finally edged past the opposition, thanks in large part to the work of Mercedes Mone, Willow Nightingale, Thekla, and a tag team division featuring Divine Dominion and The Brawling Birds.

There is more consistency up and down the roster than what we are getting from WWE today, which has been bogged down in repetition and adversely affected by significant injuries, including a knee injury suffered by Ripley.

To be fair, neither product has mastered pacing.

AEW often has so much happening on any given episode of Dynamite that it is hard to keep up. Through its seven year history, it has yet to embrace the idea of letting things breathe so the audience can absorb everything it has thrown at it.

With that said, the pacing of WWE shows since the Netflix debut in January 2025 has become insufferable.

Ad breaks, on a premium live event, are beyond frustrating and hurt the flow of the show. Look no further than WrestleMania 42, where the Saturday night portion of the annual Showcase of the Immortals featured 126 minutes of wrestling and 112 minutes of ads, just 12 minutes fewer in commercial time than in-ring content.

It has plagued WWE and, for some, made the viewing experience unbearable.

While neither has struck a perfect balance, there is little to no down time with the current AEW product, allowing fans to feel like they did not waste their time or energy to sit through a two-hour episode of Dynamite or a four-hour pay-per-view.

AEW in 2026 is a better product, both in-ring and creatively, than WWE.

That might be a hot take to some but anyone watching both shows with any regularity or consistency would likely come to the same conclusion.

Whereas WWE's in-ring content has been strong, particularly in the main event scene, AEW has been more consistent across the board. That is not particularly surprising and, with the exception of the red-hot 2023-24 period under Chief Content Officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque, the Tony Khan-owned company has always been focused, above all, on the in-ring content.

This year, the storytelling has caught up.

While still not perfect, it is more focused, with what appears to be a long-term plan involving the AEW World Championship and MJF at the top of the card. Add in a concentrated effort to elevate Kevin Knight, a spotlight on the deepest tag team division in the company, and a talented women's division getting the attention and opportunity it has earned, and you have a show that is finally realizing its potential.

Yes, WWE is still outselling its competition and making boatloads of money from sponsors, and ad sales. It has also dealt with backlash from its horrendously unsatisfying creative push to WrestleMania 42, not to mention fan frustration over the abundance of commercials over the course of a three hour premium live event.

A show no longer focused primarily on telling stories and producing great wrestling, it has been surpassed in 2026 from an overall quality standpoint. At least for the time being.

articles.title: 6 vague Arizona Cardinals injury updates from HC Mike LaFleur
articles.summary: There is no official injury report until next week, so LaFleur didn't offer much in terms of injury updates.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals have a jog-through Wednesday and then a regular practice Thursday, which will be the last on-field work until preparation begins on Labor Day for the season opener against the Los Angeles Chargers.

When this schedule was put in place by the NFL, it was mandated that all players have off from Friday through Sunday.

Head coach Mike LaFleur provided some updates with scant details this week for players that are dealing with injuries.

The veteran running back was placed on injured reserve Sunday with the ability to return later this season. Recovering from a serious ankle injury suffered early in the 2025 season, Conner was not placed on active/physically unable to perform when training camp opened.

He participated in drills, but was not part of 11-on-11 work all summer.

Was Conner close to avoiding IR, during which he can't practice and the earliest he can work and eventually play is after the fourth game?

LaFleur insisted, "He's not far off, but it just was in the best interest of the player and the organization to give him a little bit more time."

All summer, LaFleur said Conner will know when he's ready to play again.

"I don't overly ask him like you just know he's earned the right with all that," he said Monday. "So we just thought it was in the best interest, he thought it was in the best interest to get a little bit more time.

NFL insider Mike Garafolo reported that Love is 50-50 to be able to play in Week 1. That actually coincides with what we reported after the injury when Dr. David Chao (@profootballdoc) told CardsWire that a low-grade high-ankle sprain can sideline a player for 2-to-4 weeks. Two weeks after the injury was Aug. 27, while four weeks is Sept. 10, which is three days before the game against the Chargers.

When asked if he's confident if Love will play in Week 1, LaFleur hedged by saying, "Confident that he is progressing really well. So, he's taken another step. Took a step yesterday (Sunday). He'll take another step today (Monday).

The slot corner came off the active/PUP list Aug. 20 and LaFleur also used the "progressing" description for him.

"Progressing well," the head coach said. "He's in good spirits. He loves ball. He loves being out there. So we're just kind of ramping up accordingly."

As for being able to play in Week 1, he acknowledged, "I think it'll lead up all the way into Week 1."

Sean Murphy-Bunting had been working in the slot through most of the preseason, but he was released Sunday. Even if Williams is able to get on the field against the Chargers, it's difficult to imagine him getting a full complement of snaps.

LaFleur said Denzel Burke has been working inside the last two or weeks, so that appears to indicate the coaching staff has confidence in Max Melton, who regressed last season and also had some injury issues.

The starting right guard has an ankle injury and didn't make the trip to Green Bay for the joint practice and final preseason game.

LaFleur didn't have to use the "progressing" word again because the question to him asked if Adams is progressing, to which he said, "He is. He's doing well."

As for not traveling to Green Bay, LaFleur said, "We think the best treatment plan for Isaiah was just keeping him off that flight and stuff like that, being here and working with our team that was here."

Similar to Williams, the coach said that would also "go right into Week 1" in terms of a potential game-day decision.

After suffering an injury to his ribs on Aug. 6 in the Hall of Fame Game, Beck is back "full go" in practice this week. "Obviously, we're not tackling or anything like that, but he'll be ready to roll," LaFleur said.

When asked Tuesday if he was able to pick up where he left off at the time of the injury, LaFleur said, "I don't think anyone typically can pick up where they left off. But I thought he did well (Monday). It's been a few weeks since he played and just like any other position, it'll take time just to get back into that comfort and doing his responsibility with what we're asking him to do."

Johnson was selected in the second round of the 2025 draft thanks to an injury history in college and then missed five games for the Cardinals.

It's believed Johnson has an ankle injury although LaFleur said only that it's "just a lower-body injury. We'll call it that. I'm going to stick to hockey right there because I can."

Yes he can until regular-season injury reports begin, although some believe the league media medical information policy requires more. However, it doesn't mean that's what a coach has to do.

As for plans for Johnson in practice, LaFleur said (you guessed it), "We'll be smart with him in terms of what we're doing this week, but he is progressing well."

articles.title: Tiger Woods pleads guilty to lesser charge in Florida court
articles.summary: Tiger Woods, the professional golf legend, arrived in court in Martin County for a change of plea hearing stemming from an earlier arrest.
articles.body:
MARTIN COUNTY — Tiger Woods, the professional golf legend, has pleaded guilty to a lesser charge at a change of plea hearing in court in Martin County on Sept. 2.

A case docket calls it a "change of plea," which often occur when a defendant has agreed to plead no contest and potentially a sentence can be imposed.

However, an associated case document filed by Woods' attorney, Douglas Duncan, describes it as a "plea conference." Duncan represented Woods in a 2017 DUI case in Palm Beach County.

It is mandatory that defendants appear in person at a change of plea hearing.

It is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. before County Judge Darren Steele.

In addition to being arrested, Woods was issued a traffic citation related to careless driving, which carries a $163 civil penalty, records show. That case also is scheduled for a Sept. 2 change of plea.

A judge April 1 approved Woods' request to travel out of the country to start "comprehensive inpatient treatment" after the arrest, according to court records.

See photos from Tiger Woods' rollover car crash on Jupiter Island

Woods was accused of crossing a double line while driving a Land Rover on Jupiter Island and striking a trailer attached to a pickup traveling in front of him.

Woods' sport utility vehicle rolled onto the driver's side.

Following the crash, medication was discussed or mentioned by investigators and Woods, records show.

Woods agreed to participate in field sobriety exercises. Investigators instructed Woods to take off his sunglasses. His eyes were glassy and bloodshot, and his pupils "extremely dilated," records show.

He was described as "sweating profusely" when speaking with investigators after the crash.

Woods reported he had not consumed any alcoholic beverages.

Asked if he took any prescription medication, Woods said, "I take a few."

He said "he takes medication for high blood pressure, cholesterol, ibuprofen and Vicodin."

Ibuprofen can treat mild to moderate pain, arthritis or inflammation, according to Cleveland Clinic. A prescription painkiller, Vicodin contains hydrocodone and acetaminophen, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration.

Woods told investigators he took his prescription medication earlier in the morning.

Following additional exercises, investigators determined Woods' "normal faculties were impaired, and he was unable to safely operate the motor vehicle," an affidavit shows.

Woods was told he was under arrest. Investigators reported finding two hydrocodone pills in his pants pocket. Hydrocodone is a prescription painkiller.

After the rollover crash, Woods was taken to the Martin County Jail, his arrest affidavit states. Staff requested Woods get "medical clearance from the hospital" because he was in a traffic crash.

He was taken to the hospital and "refused all medical treatment," the affidavit states. "After being medically discharged, Woods was transported back to the Martin County Jail."

At the Martin County Jail, Woods took a breath test to measure blood-alcohol content. That test twice measured 0.00. A reading of 0.08 and greater is considered illegal.

Steele in earlier court actions ordered that Woods' prescription records be provided to prosecutors and ordered to allow a request for Woods' March 27 hospital records from Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital.

articles.title: There can only be 1 reason Matthew Stafford wasn't voted NFL's top QB
articles.summary: Josh Allen was voted the NFL's best QB on the Top 100 Players list, but Matthew Stafford should've finished higher.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have the MVP on their roster, but there is a continued narrative going around stating that Matthew Stafford wasn't the best quarterback in the league last season. It's a notion that was reinforced by the fact that Stafford was ranked as the fourth-best player in the NFL on the Top 100 Players list, which means Buffalo Bills superstar Josh Allen will finish above him.

Despite the fact that Stafford finished the season as the NFL's leader in passing yards and touchdowns, there are two ideas that exist preventing the Rams' quarterback from being at the top of the list. One is the weapons surrounding him. Another is something that not many are willing to talk about. Unlike his fellow contemporaries, Stafford, in the current environment, gets discredited because he's not a dual-threat quarterback.

What else could it be? How could Allen be ranked over a passer who exceeded his output? The argument that Stafford is in a better system doesn't work, as Allen is also in an efficient offense with Buffalo promoting their offensive coordinator Joe Brady to the head coaching position. The system is also custom-designed for Allen as well, negating any counter-argument about scheme.

One could say Stafford has better teammates, except the Bills have James Cook, who led the NFL in rushing yards, allowing Allen to utilize his talents to the max. Cook is as important to Allen as Puka Nacua is to Stafford. One could talk about Davante Adams, but Allen's ability as a runner makes up for it. At least it should if he's supposed to be the best quarterback in the league.

Let's think back to the 2025 MVP race. Despite there being zero logical reason for the vote to be as close as it was, Stafford edged out New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye by one single vote. The Super Bowl proved that had the vote gone the other way, it would have been one of the most outrageous decisions in recent football history. What did Maye do better?

Stafford was discredited for the Rams being pass-heavy in the red zone, with the team choosing to pass inside the 5-yard line at an incredibly high rate . Some say that's stat-padding. Those who do make that argument have never attempted to throw against an NFL defense, especially within the limited space of the end zone. It's a point that simply makes no sense, especially as the Rams entered the 2025 season with a terrible red zone offense from the season before.

So, why isn't Stafford ranked as the top quarterback in the NFL when he clearly has been? He can't run fast. That's literally it.

The narrative about Stafford will always be skewed until someone addresses the perceived bias against pocket passers.

articles.title: Sam Darnold snubbed at No. 100 as ESPN Buries Seahawks' super bowl winner before title defense
articles.summary: Darnold won a Super Bowl and matched Brady's back-to-back 14-win feat. So why does ESPN's 2026 top 100 rank Seattle's QB dead last at No. 100?
articles.body:
Landing dead last on ESPN's list of the top 100 NFL players for 2026 is a strange fate for a quarterback who just lifted a Lombardi Trophy. Yet that is exactly where Seattle's Sam Darnold sits.

A dozen ESPN analysts and reporters built the ranking around what they expect in 2026 rather than what a player has already banked, which is how a 14-3 record, an NFC crown, and a championship end up buried at the bottom of the ledger.

Seahawks beat writer Brady Henderson wrote the note attached to Darnold's placement, and it read less like a takedown than a backhanded compliment.

"No quarterback has more wins over the past two seasons than Darnold, who has 31 with the Vikings and Seahawks," Henderson wrote . "He'd be higher on this list if not for his league-high 20 turnovers in 2025, though he went the final four games without one. One reason Darnold could be better in 2026: This is the first time since 2020 that he returns to the same team as its unquestioned starter."

Those turnovers are the anchor dragging his stock down, and 20 of them are nothing to wave away. ESPN's own forecast for the coming year has him at 4,013 yards, 24 scores, and 12 picks, numbers that would satisfy plenty of franchises but feel oddly small for a reigning champion.

Two 14-Win Seasons in a Row Put Darnold in Company, Only Tom Brady Has Kept

Continuity has been the missing ingredient across Darnold's career , and 2026 finally hands it to him. He turns 29 entering his second year in Mike Macdonald's system, the front office paid Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Leonard Williams to keep the core intact, and reinforcements arrived around a championship roster.

The resume backing all of this is loud. Darnold went 14-3 as Seattle's starter after posting an identical 14-3 mark in Minnesota, and stacking two 14-win campaigns back-to-back has been done by exactly one other quarterback in league history: Tom Brady, in 2003 and 2004.

During the regular season, he threw for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns against 14 interceptions. Smith-Njigba fueled the passing game with a personal-best 1,793 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns on 119 catches and 163 targets.

The Super Bowl itself was more grind than showcase, a 19-of-38, 202-yard, one-touchdown outing in a 29-13 win over New England, with the defense and ground attack doing the heavy lifting.

Get past that box score, though, and the postseason speaks for itself: a rout of San Francisco in the divisional round, a 346-yard, three-touchdown NFC Championship win over the Rams , and zero turnovers across the entire January stretch after leading the league in them all year.

Ranking a title winner behind 99 players suggests his mistakes matter more than his results. Seattle opens its title defense Sept. 9 against the Patriots at Lumen Field.

articles.title: Clemson should move on from Dabo Swinney
articles.summary: Is Dabo's time with Clemson coming to an end?
articles.body:
Not everyone gets to go out on top. In the sport of college football , there's a bit of a spectrum for how the career comes to an end.

At the bottom, there's ending the career in utter disgrace with a national scandal like Joe Paterno, a regular old firing like what LSU did to Brian Kelly, a quiet retirement like Duke's David Cutcliffe, making one last run and then bowing out like Nick Saban, and then at the very top, winning a National Championship and riding off into the sunset like Jim Harbaugh.

So, how will it end for Dabo Swinney at Clemson? And will it happen this season?

Clemson corner back Ashton Hampton (2) looks as Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney walks by during practice in the at the Allen N. Reeves Sports Complex in Clemson, S.C. Friday, August 7, 2026.

Dabo seems to have lost his fastball. After taking over as the interim head coach in 2008 after Tommy Bowden's firing, Dabo Swinney slowly built Clemson into a national power, winning a BCS Bowl after the 2012 season. But in 2014, when Clemson landed Deshaun Watson, who was the top-ranked quarterback in the country, Clemson's reputation, and Dabo's, changed instantly.

Dabo went from just a goofy "good ole boy" football coach to an incredibly quotable and endlessly entertaining character. Clemson went from being just a good ACC program to a National Championship contender. Nothing exemplifies the arrival of both Dabo and his football team better than the "Bring Your Own Guts" game in 2015, where Clemson beat a top-10 ranked Notre Dame in a driving rainstorm thanks to a late two-point conversion stop.

Over the next six seasons, Clemson would qualify for the 4-team College Football Playoff every season, and win two National Championships. After Watson left for the NFL, Swinney backfilled by recruiting (and winning a Championship with) Trevor Lawrence, another all-time great QB prospect from the state of Georgia.

But ever since Trevor Lawrence left, Clemson hasn't been the same, and frankly, so has Dabo. His endless quotability has worked against him, as he has often been taken out of context and seemingly behind the times on modern political issues, with reporters almost baiting him into saying something that could be viewed in bad taste.

As college football transitioned into the transfer portal and NIL era, Dabo has continued to try to build teams through old school loyalty and high school recruiting. It hasn't worked. Since Trevor Lawrence became a Jacksonville Jaguar, Clemson has won the ACC only once, qualified for only one College Football Playoff (as a 12-seed), won no CFP games, and never finished in the top-10 of the final AP poll.

Clemson's quarterback problem is Dabo's problem

You see the trend, right? Dabo Swinney has been directly tied to his quarterbacks. Good quarterback? National Championship contender. Bad quarterback? Hello, Pinstripe Bowl.

So, the question is, where does Clemson's QB room stand heading into 2026? If you let Dabo tell you, not great. Dabo Swinney has been repeatedly out in press conferences complaining about his roster and not being willing to reveal who his starters are.

That doesn't bode well for a team that is going to be at a vast talent disadvantage on Saturday, as Clemson travels to Death Valley to take on LSU.

So, should Clemson move on from Dabo? That depends – how good is his quarterback? And if the quarterback isn't good this year, how many more opportunities do you give him to find one?

Because that is going to make all the difference in whether he exits like Brian Kelly or like Nick Saban.

articles.title: NHL Odds ‘n Ends: Hellebuyck, expansion, Jagr finished?
articles.summary: The latest official Team USA to trade request is goalie Connor Hellebuyck. Before anyone asks, there’s no reason to expect he would be in Pittsburgh’s intere...
articles.body:
The latest official Team USA to trade request is goalie Connor Hellebuyck. Before anyone asks, there's no reason to expect he would be in Pittsburgh's interests- or more importantly nor would they be on his list. The Athletic recently listed eight possibilities of teams that might make sense, and the Penguins were nowhere to be found. That about sums it up. Here's some of the most widely speculated destinations.

Buffalo, Carolina and New Jersey are among the most common – and that wouldn't be welcome for the Penguins if Hellebuyck ends up in the division like the Hurricanes or Devils. There are enough top goalies in the Metropolitan already , for cryin' out loud!

Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin's situations are interesting, how awkward it'll be if they can't be moved before the season starts. Everyone knows they want out, from the fans to their teammates and everyone around the organization. Their hearts aren't in it anymore, yet they've signed to play for NHL clubs who haven't felt like they've gotten a good trade offer yet. How those stalemate plays out will be fun to watch from afar. It could escalate even further, with some chatter picking up that Hellebuyck might not report to training camp at all and start one of the first hold outs the NHL has seen in a long, long time for a contracted player.

Sergei Murashov got a passing mention (at No. 12) for potential Calder Trophy contenders this season.

Overall, not to be a downer, but it's probably even more unlikely than that. A goalie hasn't won the rookie of the year award in the NHL since Steve Mason in 2009. The Penguins have a very casual relationship with all things defensively when it comes to limiting shots and chances of opponents. Nice to see Murashov on the radar and getting a smidge of national attention, if nothing else.

NHL expansion is all but confirmed to be coming again, perhaps as soon as Houston for the 2029-30 season .

The NHL has so many Canadian teams that they still have some really big areas in America to go after and try and raise their market share of fans. Adding teams in places like Houston, Atlanta and maybe even Phoenix would bring in huge, untapped markets. Being the first major North American pro league to go beyond 32 franchises is bold, but with the prices they are getting these days, it's a no-brainer to keep growing.

What the means for the future will be interesting, most the headway seems to be pointing to going to 36 eventually, and the league reportedly doesn't care about being unbalanced with 33 teams. Perhaps eventually they'll split into six divisions of six teams and feature more geographic rivals.

Jaromir Jagr, who the Penguins traded 25 years ago this summer, looks like he is finally completed his circuit as a player. For real this time.

Jagr left the NHL in the 2017-18 season – playing for his hometown Kladno Knights in Czechia ever sense. It's been a long drawn-down with him playing sparingly recently (Jags only played 15 games in 2023-24, and just six last season in 2025-26), but I mean he's been 50+ years old so what can you expect? Most of his recent playing has been to drive interest at the box office for the perpetually struggling team that he once partially owned to try and make ends meet financially, while also winning enough to avoid relegation out of the primary pro league- not terribly different from Jagr's efforts in the late '90s with Pittsburgh.

Along the way, he enjoyed every minute of the struggle. Next stop could finally be Toronto for the Hockey Hall of Fame if he truly is done as an active player.
