articles.title: Oregon aiming to tighten series history vs. Boise State
articles.summary: Oregon doesn't have the best track record against Boise State, but Saturday's matchup offers a chance to tighten the series record.
articles.body:
Given the proximity of the two programs, it's a bit surprising how little the Oregon Ducks have shared the field with Boise State in the past. On Sept. 5, the Ducks and Broncos will do battle for just the fifth time, and the Ducks have some work to do to get even in the series.

Boise State has a 3-1 series edge over Oregon, but every game in the series has been a close fight. Oregon holds the longest nonconference home win streak in the country, with 38 straight victories dating back to 2009. The most recent loss? Well, that came against Boise State, which beat the Ducks 37-32 on Sept. 20, 2008.

That marked the first game in series history between Oregon and Boise State. The Ducks lost starting quarterback Jeremiah Masoli early in that matchup as the Broncos pulled off the upset at Autzen Stadium. Oregon and Boise State met up again the following season, this time on the infamous blue turf in Boise, Idaho. The Ducks fell, 19-8, in a game that famously ended with LeGarrette Blount throwing a punch at Boise State's Bryan Hout.

The two programs didn't meet again until 2017, when Boise State beat the Ducks, 38-28, in the Las Vegas Bowl. Oregon entered the game under unusual circumstances, with former head coach Willie Taggart having left the program before the game, beginning the Mario Cristobal era.

Royce Freeman sat out the game in preparation for the NFL draft, while freshman quarterback Justin Herbert tossed two touchdowns and a pair of interceptions in the loss. A few years later, the core of that team, led by Herbert and linebacker Troy Dye , went on to win the Pac-12 and the Rose Bowl. While many Oregon fans might choose to forget this bowl loss, it was an important learning opportunity and a moment the Ducks used to build upon.

Oregon finally picked up its first win ever over Boise State in 2024, but it was much closer than many had expected. The Ducks were favored by three scores, but still needed a pair of special teams touchdowns and a walk-off field goal by Atticus Sappington to escape with a 37-34 victory.

Evan Stewart shined with five catches for 112 yards and a touchdown, while Boise State quarterback Maddux Madsen struggled, completing just 17-of-40 pass attempts. Ashton Jeanty carved the Ducks' defense apart, rushing for 192 yards and three touchdowns en route to a Heisman finalist campaign. Stewart and Madsen will both take the field again on Saturday.

With a win, Oregon can create its first winning streak over Boise State. The Ducks have been great in season openers, particularly at home, winning the last 21 home openers in Eugene. The Broncos and Ducks have split their only two matchups at Autzen Stadium, but the Ducks are big favorites again this weekend.

Oregon and Boise State are both vying for playoff spots this season, and the Ducks have a distinct talent advantage in terms of blue-chip players on the roster. articles.title: Yankees At-Bat(s) of the Week: Ali Sánchez, Paul Goldschmidt, and Heliot Ramos (8/30)
articles.summary: The Yankees’ romp of the Red Sox started with a clutch sequence of at-bats in the fifth.
articles.body:
In arguably their most important game of the season, the Yankees bats showed up to play. On Sunday, the offense steamrolled the Red Sox, 16-1 , to take three out of four and win the season series. In a game full of quality at-bats, there was a sequence of three in the fifth inning that set them on course for the eventual blow out — a perfect sacrifice bunt by Ali Sánchez, a two-run single by Paul Goldschmidt to reap the reward of Sánchez's bunt, and the game-breaking three-run homer from Heliot Ramos.

We join Sánchez with no outs in the bottom of the fifth. Runs are hard to come by with Will Warren and Ranger Suarez both dealing. However, the Yankees have a golden opportunity with runners on first and second after José Caballero led off with a single and Jazz Chisholm Jr. followed with a shallow fly to right-center that was controversially ruled to be trapped instead of caught by Ceddanne Rafaela — a decision upheld after replay showed no decisive angle to overturn . Sensing that the Red Sox were still reeling from that perceived injustice, it became imperative for the Yankees to strike during this moment of weakness from the opponent.

Everyone in the stadium knows before Sánchez even dug in that there was one objective on his mind — a well-executed sac bunt to move both runners into scoring position. Suarez understands this and selects a pitch that should be difficult to bunt cleanly — a cutter up and in.

Suarez gets the pitch to his spot, burying this cutter in on Sánchez's hands. However, Sánchez does an even better job of positioning and angling the bat early to cushion the ball down the third base line rather than having to stab at the pitch. The result is a perfectly placed bunt that moves both runners up for a hitter who absolutely crushes lefties.

Next up is Goldschmidt. When facing lefties, he seems to have a defined plan — hunt fastballs inside that he can pull for power early in the count before going with an right-center field approach after falling behind.

After sticking with mostly soft stuff the first two times he faced Goldschmidt, Suarez goes right at him in this AB with fastballs, starting with this four-seamer up.

This heater is pretty much over the plate, but it's elevated just high enough and Goldschmidt is just late enough with his swing that he's only able to foul it back over the screen.

Suarez stays on the attack with another four-seamer.

This time, Goldschmidt is ready for the pitch and starts his swing earlier. Even though this is a much better located pitch in off the plate to partially handcuff Goldschmidt, he's strong enough to muscle this ground ball up the middle through the pulled-in infield to plate both base runners. He got the pitch he was looking for and just missed it and made sure not to miss it when the second one came.

After Cody Bellinger singled to put runners on first and second, Ramos steps to the plate in one of the biggest spots of his brief Yankees career looking for his first true signature Yankees moment.

When Suarez faced Ramos in the first inning, he busted him inside with all fastballs. It's the same story here, starting with this first-pitch four-seamer.

This pitch is perfectly located, painted on the inside edge low. Even if Ramos had used an ABS challenge, it would have confirmed this as a called strike.

Suarez looks to replicate that execution with his next pitch.

You can see the way the previous called strike tempts Ramos to chase this fastball in off the plate. However, he checks his swing in time as he recognizes that Suarez has pulled this four-seamer a littler further inside.

After establishing a pair of heaters inside, the obvious sequence would be to follow with a back-foot slider. If he can throw it down the same tunnel as the previous two fastballs, Ramos should have a very hard time not chasing.

Suarez executes the exact pitch he intends and it takes decent concentration from Ramos to track the movement and fight it off foul to stay alive.

With Ramos showing a willingness to swing at the breaking ball down and in, Suarez opts for the slower and greater breaking curveball hoping to get the hitter out in front for the swinging strikeout.

Ramos is sitting on the bender and matches his swing path and timing perfectly to rope a three-run shot into the bleachers in left. It's by no means a bad pitch given it's on the corner down and in. However, the previous slider got Ramos hunting breaking ball, so as a pitcher you have to bury the following breaker almost in the dirt. You can almost see the weeks of frustration melt away with each step Ramos takes around the bases.

As much as I am generally not a fan of bunting, I have to concede that Sánchez's sacrifice was the turning point of the game following the controversial call on Rafaela. Then came the crafty veteran experience of Goldschmidt hunting the fastball in against the lefty and not missing when he got his pitch. Finally, there was the emotional release of the home run which seemed to lift the weight of the world off Ramos' shoulders — a moment which can make any player feel truly a part of their new team after joining midseason and not immediately producing. Some unlikely heroes stepped up in one of the biggest moments of the Yankees season, and it was almost like Boston waved the white flag once Ramos' ball left the yard, culminating in the eventual blowout.

articles.title: The date Scottie Scheffler can surpass Tiger Woods’ record for most consecutive weeks as world No.1
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is one of the two greatest golfers ever to have played the game alongside Jack Nicklaus, but Scottie Scheffler now has his sights set on one of t...
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is one of the two greatest golfers ever to have played the game alongside Jack Nicklaus, but Scottie Scheffler now has his sights set on one of the 15-time major champion's all-time records.

Woods won 82 times on the PGA Tour, while Scheffler has 22 victories to his name so far.

The 50-year-old is a huge admirer of the four-time major champion's game, and it's little wonder, given his domination of the sport since 2022.

Scottie Scheffler may not be on the same level as Tiger Woods was in his prime, but he's certainly on the right trajectory.

Comparisons have often been made between Scheffler and Woods , mainly because of the drive, hunger and fierce competitiveness that they both possess.

The current world number one is actually hunting down one of Woods' most impressive career records.

When Scottie Scheffler can surpass Tiger Woods' world rankings record

There is no doubt that the 30-year-old from Dallas, Texas, will go down as one of the greatest golfers of all time when he retires.

And he's on track to do something that was unthinkable before he burst onto the scene.

He has currently been world number one for 172 consecutive weeks.

If Scheffler is still world number one on the 15th October 2028, he will have been at the top of the pile for 282 consecutive weeks.

Woods' record of consecutive weeks as world number one stands at 281 weeks, from 12th June 2005 through to 30th October 2010.

The gap between Scheffler and world number two Rory McIlroy in the rankings is greater than the one between the Northern Irishman and the bottom ranked player in professional golf.

So there is a good chance that the 30-year-old Texan will still be world number one in two years' time, even if he plays average golf over the next two seasons.

Scottie Scheffler's pursuit of Tiger Woods' all-time world No.1 record

While the consecutive weeks record should be attainable for Scheffler, Woods' record of total weeks spent as world No.1 will be harder to beat.

The 15-time major champion spent 683 weeks in total as the number one ranked golfer in the world.

Scheffler has currently been world number one for 207 weeks in total.

That means that the earliest possible date that the Texan will be able to overtake Woods' record will be in October 2035!

Scheffler will be 39 then, so there's a chance that he will be able to maintain his current form over the next nine years.

However, it will obviously be incredibly difficult for him to do that, as talented young players continue to emerge on the PGA Tour every single season.

Of course, Woods' record of 683 weeks is a total number, so Scheffler won't have to remain at the top for the next nine years in order to beat the great man's achievement.

October 2035 is just the earliest possible date that the 22-time PGA Tour winner will be able to surpass the 15-time major champion's record.

articles.title: 'I'll bet on this' - Vrancken backs Braga to stay at Hearts
articles.summary: Head coach Wouter Vrancken would wager on Claudio Braga remaining at Hearts and thinks a second full season at Tynecastle can enhance the striker's chances o...
articles.body:
Head coach Wouter Vrancken would wager on Claudio Braga remaining at Hearts and thinks a second full season at Tynecastle can enhance the striker's chances of a big move.

"He is fully focused here, fully committed," said the Belgian of the 26-year-old.

When asked if the Portuguese would still be at the club when the transfer window closes on Thursday, Vrancken added with a chuckle: "I think he will be here. I'll bet on this.

"But you never know, so let's hope that we can keep him because he has a lot of value for the team."

Braga has scored twice and provided three assists in 10 outings this term while he hit the net 17 times during his first campaign in Edinburgh, having been signed from the Norwegian second tier.

"He's important because he has quality," said Vranken. "He is also coachable and thinks about the team. He has the mindset that the team is the most important thing. For me, that's an extra reason to want to keep him.

"It can be a good thing for him to stay and show himself in a different style of play because the bigger teams are not looking for a player who does one good year in a certain style of play."

It has been a busy summer of change for Hearts, with Vranken replacing Derek McInnes and 14 new signings to compensate for 12 departures.

"I would never say settled because I know what can happen in the last seconds of such a window," said the head coach of any late transfer activity before Thursday's derby with Hibernian at Easter Road.

"We are discussing possibilities all the time, incoming, outgoing."

articles.title: The Athletic shares concern about Panthers' defense in 2026
articles.summary: Robert Mays of The Athletic questions if the Panthers will be able to finally ignite their pass rush in 2026.
articles.body:
The biggest question facing the Carolina Panthers going into the 2026 season is how much quarterback Bryce Young will improve compared to last season. On the other side of the ball, the big unanswered question is if their pass rush can finally claw their way out of the NFL's basement after a bottom-five finish in sacks three years running.

To their credit, the Panthers went out of their way to improve their defensive front seven in free agency, signing edge rusher Jaelan Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd, a great pass rusher for his position, to huge deals.

Now, can defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero get this group up to a respectable level in the all-important pass-rushing category? That's what The Atheltic's NFL analyst Robert Mays will be watching for in the first month of the season:

Is Jaelan Phillips enough to take that pass rush from a team that finished 32nd when rushing four to a unit that feels dangerous? Because that's about more than individual talent, and he really is the only guy you're adding back into that. Turk Wharton is still hurt. You lose Nic Scourton before the season. There are some teams that even if they don't have the horses pass-rush wise, the plan feels dynamic.

Wharton didn't do much in this department last year even when he was on the field, but losing Scourton for the season is an undeniably painful blow to the Panthers' front. As of yet, they haven't added a dynamic option to replace him on the edge, leaving a lot of pressure on Pat Jones II and Princely Umanmielen to step up at the spot opposite Phillips.

As Mays mentions, it's about more than just the personnel, here. Evero has been extremely reluctant to blitz the quarterback during his run as the Panthers' defensive coordinator. He did have success doing so against the Los Angeles Rams in their playoff matchup—and will need to consider embracing it more often if he's going to generate the kind of pressure the Panthers need to compete.

articles.title: Kam Perry returns ahead of Colorado's opener vs. Georgia Tech
articles.summary: Kam Perry's return from an elbow injury gives Colorado a key weapon for Thursday's season opener against Georgia Tech.
articles.body:
Kam Perry's return to Colorado Buffaloes practice has changed the outlook for the Buffaloes' receiving corps ahead of Thursday's season opener at Georgia Tech . The senior wide receiver was back in a yellow, non-contact jersey Aug. 26 after missing roughly two weeks with an elbow injury.

Deion Sanders has remained optimistic about Perry's availability. The 5-foot-9, 170-pound receiver is expected to suit up when Colorado visits Georgia Tech on Sept. 3 , giving quarterback Julian Lewis a proven downfield target.

Perry produced 43 receptions for 976 yards and six touchdowns at Miami (Ohio) in 2025. His 22.7 yards per catch ranked third nationally, and he earned First-Team All-MAC honors along with Miami's Offensive MVP award.

Perry's return to practice last week is a gradual ramp-up before kickoff. The yellow practice jersey allowed him to participate in drills without taking full contact, as he was still wearing a brace on his left arm.

Many practice clips from the first week of fall camp in Colorado Springs showed Perry with exceptional agility and quickness. Colorado coaches have a few days to determine Perry's workload in the game, as a managed snap count remains possible, with the expectation that he will be included in important offensive packages.

Perry began his college career at Indiana , where he recorded three receptions for 22 yards across two seasons. He transferred to Miami (Ohio) and made an immediate contribution in 2024 with 10 catches for 166 yards.

His breakout came the following year. Perry started 12 games and became one of the nation's most dangerous big-play receivers.

Perry also brings value inside the formation. Roughly 60% of his snaps came from the slot last season, where his acceleration and route timing helped him create separation. His run-blocking skills also show his willingness to contribute when Colorado has the ball on the ground.

Brennan Marion's offense gives Perry room to work from the slot and outside. His speed can stretch a defense vertically, and his short-area quickness creates opportunities on underneath routes.

Danny Scudero Jr., DeAndre Moore, Joseph Williams and Cam Perry all give Colorado a deep group of skill-position options when healthy. Georgia Tech 's secondary will have to account for Perry's alignment on every series.

Perry's return also gives Lewis another receiver with proven production. His ability to win individual matchups could become one of Colorado's most important offensive storylines Thursday night .

articles.title: Broncos still like their OLB depth even without Jonathon Cooper
articles.summary: Even without Jonathon Cooper, the Denver Broncos still have strong depth at outside linebacker.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos have lost one of their top defensive players to start the season, but it doesn't seem like the team is sounding off any alarms.

Just as teams were finalizing their 53-man rosters ahead of Sunday's deadline, it was announced that outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper was placed on the commissioner's exempt list to begin the season. This, of course, stems from a pair of arrests after alleged domestic violence incidents in June. As a result, he cannot practice with the team or play in any games as long as he is on that list.

This will force the Broncos to turn to third-year player Jonah Elliss in his absence, and both Que Robinson and Dondrea Tillman could get into games as situational pass rushers as well. However, that doesn't seem to bother general manager George Paton.

"These guys have all played in big games and done well," Paton said on his trust level in the outside linebacker depth with Elliss, Robinson and Tillman. "All these guys we feel like can play. We like the depth there. We led the league in sacks the last two years, and these guys were all a part of that. Que coming on late. I think you saw what Que did in the New England game late in the season, even the Houston game last year and some of the things he did.

"Then you watched him in training camp and the games this year. We feel really good about him. Then Jonah and obviously 'Tilly' and Nik, these guys have played and have done well. Depth-wise, we'll be looking a little bit, looking on the practice squad and we'll be looking around. You can never have enough pass rushers, so we'll kind of see how that goes".

Broncos could look at free agency or practice squads for help

Some of the top veteran free-agent options at outside linebacker include Haasan Reddick, Kyle Van Noy and Leonard Floyd. All of those players have shown the ability to create havoc on defense and while they may no longer be every-down players, they might be solid options until Cooper's situation is resolved.

On their own practice squad , the Broncos have Johnny Walker and international pathway player David Agoha. Agoha is nowhere near ready to play in an NFL game, but Walker could be an option in a desperate situation. The Broncos will likely also scour the practice squads around the league in search of a potential option to poach from another team.

It will be interesting to see how things play out, but it should be expected that the Broncos will roll with what they have until Cooper returns.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz hindered by ‘unique’ US Open rule
articles.summary: Alcaraz is returning from four months out with a wrist injury as he tries to defend his title at Flushing Meadows but will the balls used cause an issue?
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz could be hindered by a rule that is unique to the US Open as the Spaniard seeks an eighth grand slam title at Flushing Meadows over the next fortnight .

Having spent the last four months sidelined by a wrist injury suffered at the Barcelona Open in April, Alcaraz is making his return to singles action at Flushing Meadows and came through his first-round match against Russia's Roman Safiullin 6-4 6-4 6-4 earlier this week.

The seven-time grand slam champion next faces Portugal's Jaime Faria in this evening's session as he looks to move another step closer to a third US Open crown – having lifted the trophy in 2022 and last year .

Playing tennis at an elite level again after a wrist issue will always be fraught but Alcaraz arguably faces an even greater challenge this fortnight, given that the men's events at Flushing Meadows use a heavier tennis ball than the women's competitions in New York.

Speaking about the issue, Sky Sports pundit Tim Henman explained: "At Wimbledon they (the men and women) use the same ball. At the Australian Open, and all other tournaments they use the same ball.

"I think it's somewhat unique to this event. For a while, the men and women did use the same ball here but I think it was a request from the WTA because the women used the extra-duty felt and they didn't like it so much, so they went back to the normal ball."

And Henman's fellow pundit Naomi Broady believes the different ball could pose a problem for Alcaraz and others who have previously suffered wrist injuries in particular.

Broady said: "I think for me as well, it does intertwine with the conversation on the ATP Tour regarding the injuries and how many wrist injuries they have and should they be playing with a ball that is heavier? Would they be better off with a lighter ball?

"You're then going to have shorter rallies because it's harder to control, it's going to move faster through the air, so there serves are going to be bigger, it's going to be tougher to get returns and extend those longer rallies.

"But the way men's tennis is going and how many injuries we're seeing, I think it is a call from the players. Firstly to have a consistent ball used across the tour. There are so many variables. Not only are tennis courts changing week to week, but the ball is as well.

"So some weeks the ball is going to fly faster through the air, sometimes it's slower and you feel like it's not leaving your strings. I think the request from the men is to stop using the really heavy balls, not to say the US Open is necessarily one of them, but it's certainly heavier than the women's and I don't think it helps the likes of Alcaraz and the guys who have had those injuries."

articles.title: New Tampa Bay Rays Ballpark Closer Than Ever After Decades Of Check Swings
articles.summary: Rays' CEO Ken Babby noted he and his fellow members of the team’s ownership group would “toast a glass to Tampa, the county and the city for this incredible...
articles.body:
While seated in the Rays' dugout at Tropicana Field last Friday afternoon, and with Happy Hour on the immediate horizon, Ken Babby noted he and his fellow members of the team's ownership group would "toast a glass to Tampa, the county and the city for this incredible moment."

One can only suspect the glasses were not merely half full, but spilling over in joy as a result of a memorable couple of days that now serves as landmarks on the timeline of a franchise that was born in 1995.

With Tampa City Council and the Hillsborough County Commission having approved the agreement for the Rays' $2.36 billion ballpark – votes of 4-3 for the former and 5-2 for the latter -- as the centerpiece of a 130-acre proposed mixed-use development on the site of Hillsborough College, there was nothing but good feeling passed around along with a sense of "finally" given the long-running drama that has been the Rays' pursuance of a new home.

"Incredibly humbling," is how Babby, the team's CEO, described the process of getting to this point less than a year after he, managing partner a co-chair Patrick Zalupski, the founder of Jacksonville-based Dream Finders Homes , and co-chair Bill Cosgrove, founder and owner of Ohio-based Union Home Mortgage , were introduced to the media at Steinbrenner Field early last October. (Union Home Mortgage has visibility in Tampa as the presenting sponsor for the Gasparilla Bowl played at Raymond James Stadium.)

Steinbrenner Field was home to the Rays in 2025 following the devastation the region incurred at the expense of Hurricane Milton in October 2024, including the Tropicana Field roof being torn apart. It only added to the continuous cycle of stadium talk that has surrounded the team for years, including a split-city plan that was proposed during an embarrassment of a dog and pony show at, appropriately, the Dali Museum in 2019 on the St. Pete waterfront where surrealism was indeed front and center.

"It's two decades in the making and we appreciate the uncertainty and certainly of all of the starts and stops with the ballpark," said Babby, adding that when Rays fans go to sleep "they know the Tampa Bay Rays are here forever in Tampa."

The ownership group has expressed interest in a ballpark community similar to the Battery Atlanta complex in Cobb County, Ga., where the Braves play at Truist Park. Hillsborough County's contribution to the roughly 30,000-seat, and seating expandable, ballpark is slated to be $796 million, approximately 80 percent of which comes from community investment and tourist development taxes, the latter often referenced as a "bed tax." The city is providing roughly $80 million in public funding. The Rays will take care of the rest, approximately $1.4 billion, and will be responsible for addition costs the project may incur.

In dealing with a project of this magnitude, bumps in the road can certainly occur between now and the targeted curtain rising of Opening Day 2029. As Babby pointed out, the constituents are many and include neighboring communities, elected officials, business leaders and other sports teams – the Yankees' Steinbrenner Field is on property connected to Hillsborough College and the NFL's Buccaneers are across the street – and of course, the city and county. Celebrating? Sure. Resting easily? Not a chance.

"We will never stop listening," said Babby. "We're not going to stop just because some votes took place (last week)."

The ownership group is listening to inquiries from companies that have expressed interest in filling the office space that will be part of the mixed-use campus.

"These are businesses that are not even based in Florida," said Babby, a former chief revenue officer of the Washington Post , with which he was also general manager of the media entity's digital arm. "Now, we get a chance to go back and have authentic conversations with them about the dream and the vision becoming a reality."

As for the two-year college, which opened its doors in 1968 and has its share of outdated facilities, a $150 million commitment has come from the state. Fifty million of the commitment has been secured. Governor Ron DeSantis has been a supporter of the project and in February approved the granting of a 22-acre plot of land to the college for the purpose of redevelopment.

"We were obviously very supportive with Hillsborough College of that site," the governor said at a news conference in Tampa on August 24. "And we think it's going to be great for the college. And there's going to be a lot of opportunities there for that."

The reality is much work needs to be completed before glasses are raised at a formal groundbreaking. Bond validation, which according to Babby will be 30 to 90 days, work on the college's temporary campus, and a community benefits plan top the list. With respect to the latter, affordable housing, neighborhood investment, youth sports initiatives and the like are among critical ingredients.

"I am a big list guy, and the to-do list is deep," said Babby.

Alas, securing commitments from the county and city were vital. Otherwise, cities outside the region would be lining up in earnest to take on a relocating franchise. Instead, this is the closest the Rays and the Tampa Bay region have come to getting a new ballpark.

"We are off and running," said Babby. "We have long said it has been our dream to build this 'Forever Home.'"

articles.title: Trabzonspor U-turn to accept manager's resignation
articles.summary: The Turkish club accepts the "emotional" resignation of head coach Fatih Tekke after initially rejecting his request to step down.
articles.body:
Trabzonspor have accepted the "emotional" resignation of head coach Fatih Tekke after the Turkish side initially rejected his request to step down.

Tekke, who led Trabzonspor to a third‑place finish in the league last season, tendered his resignation after his side were knocked out of the Europa League play‑off round 5‑0 on aggregate by Hungarian club Ferencvaros.

After rejecting his request on Friday and suggesting the 48‑year‑old made the decision under the "intense emotional impact" of the Europa League exit, the Super Lig club have now agreed to part ways with their head coach.

In a statement released on Wednesday, Trabzonspor said it reached a "mutual understanding" with Tekke and decided to part ways "in line with Trabzonspor's interests and long‑term objectives".

The statement added: "Over his approximately 18‑month tenure, Fatih Tekke brought significant value to Trabzonspor.

"Beyond contributing to the development of the players added to our squad during this period, he delivered important sporting and financial gains for our club. By bringing the Turkish Cup back to our museum, he once again wrote his name into Trabzonspor's history.

"At this point, we reached a mutual understanding with our coach - who stated he would never allow his presence to harm Trabzonspor in any way - that drawing a new roadmap, prioritising the club's interests above all else, had become unavoidable.

"We thank our coach for his efforts, his dedicated work, the successes he delivered, and the value he added to Trabzonspor."

Trabzonspor, who signed Mohamed Salah in the summer, will still play European football this season, in the Europa Conference League, with Scottish side Hearts among their six opponents.

The seven-time Turkish champions also signed Liverpool's Premier League winner Fabinho in the summer while goalkeeper Andre Onana has also rejoined the club on loan from Manchester United.

Salah, 34, made the shock decision to sign for Trabzonspor last month after mutually agreeing to end his contract at Liverpool last season.

The Egypt international is the third-highest scorer in the Reds' history, behind only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt, after scoring 257 goals in 442 appearances following his move from Roma in 2017.

Salah scored his first two goals for his new club in Saturday's 2-1 win against Istanbul Basaksehir.

articles.title: Failed Everton transfer has implications for Arsenal & Chelsea
articles.summary: Folarin Balogun’s transfer to Everton fell apart late on deadline day, denying Arsenal a sell-on fee and seemingly causing significant problems for Chelsea i...
articles.body:
Folarin Balogun's transfer to Everton fell apart late on deadline day, denying Arsenal a sell-on fee and seemingly causing significant problems for Chelsea in the process.

Early on deadline day, we covered reports that AS Monaco's Folarin Balogun was set to sign for Everton in a €50m package that would see Arsenal cashing in on their 17.5% sell-on clause.

Yet that move was thrown into doubt after Fabrice Hawkins reported for RMC Sport that Balogun had failed his medical.

Sami Mokbel reported for the BBC that Everton still wanted to proceed with the deal, but at a lower price. The deal was renegotiated for a lower fixed fee with higher add-ons, but David Ornstein reports for The Athletic that the player then pulled out and returned to Monaco.

The failed transfer denied Arsenal a fee in the region of £6-7.5m, but the saga also had serious implications for Chelsea.

Chelsea had hoped to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco as a replacement for Enzo Fernandez , with The Athletic reporting that they had a full written agreement in place. But after Monaco renegotiated Balogun's exit, they pulled out of the Camara deal.

Monaco evidently felt the Balogun sale would bring in enough money, and they no longer needed to sell Camara. But Balogun then pulled out of the Everton move, too late for Monaco and Chelsea to revive their transfer.

Quite why Balogun decided against the Everton transfer hasn't been reported.

It's fair to assume he might have been unhappy with how the Merseyside club conducted themselves, leaking reports of his failed medical to the media and trying to lower the transfer fee at the last minute. But he may also just have had a change of heart.

Arsenal will retain their sell-on clause for future windows, but whether Monaco receive another bid for a similar amount is far from certain. The striker's deal expires in 2028, there will be questions about this failed medical, and he won't have a World Cup showcase next summer.

Unless the 25-year-old has a fantastic 2026/27 season, it's likely a transfer next year won't hit the same figure in that context.

articles.title: Chelsea’s £500m profit numbers are impressive – but totally nonsensical
articles.summary: Chelsea made more than £500m in player sales this summer and improved their squad – but it’s a little more complicated than that.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea co...
articles.body:
Chelsea made more than £500m in player sales this summer and improved their squad – but it's a little more complicated than that.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Nizaar Kinsella has been looking back at Chelsea's summer transfers now the English window is shut.

As he points out, according to the club's own numbers, Chelsea spent £349.2m and received 437m. That means a net profit of £87.8m. There were a number of really good sales, and the squad is without doubt better now than it was a few months ago. The club think the amount received will eventually reach £500m when add-ons, loan fees and sell-on clauses are considered, improving their standing further.

Chelsea numbers don't take into account years of spending

But despite that, those number are very misleading. Counting one window's transfers in a vacuum is pretty meaningless. Yes we sold Enzo Fernandez for £125m, but we bought him for £105m. One of those numbers is reflected above, the other isn't.

Looking at this window's numbers alone we made £8m on Deivid Washington. Zoom out a little and you'll see we lost £8m on him in two years, in exchange for 25 minutes of senior football. Of course it works both ways, and we could yet sell a player we bought this summer for a huge profit.

£500m profit is nice – £450m and a £50m midfielder to help the team would have been even better.

The window reached a crazy climax with the Lamine Camara deal coming together – and then suddenly falling apart.

articles.title: How Everton's deadline day debacle leaves owners facing fan mutiny
articles.summary: Everton's transfer deadline day debacle over Folarin Balogun leaves owners The Friedkin facing fan mutiny, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Everton's shambolic end to the transfer window has resulted in open revolt from supporters that places fierce scrutiny on owners The Friedkin Group and chief executive Angus Kinnear.

The final straw for fans already infuriated by the controversial proposed sale of home-grown youngster Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest - the deal was eventually blocked by Everton's board in the face of the toxic reaction from the fanbase - was the bungled final day before the window closed.

Folarin Balogun's proposed £40m move from AS Monaco descended into high farce in the early hours of Wednesday morning after the original deal was renegotiated when issues arose with his medical, ending with the United States striker deciding to walk away from Everton's Finch Farm training base without signing.

And all after Balogun, 25, and both clubs had signed the deal sheet allowing the move to be completed after Tuesday's 23.00 BST transfer deadline.

Everton had scheduled an 8am flight to bring Balogun to Merseyside, but he was unable to arrive until later in the day. Everton were also frustrated at a delay in receiving documents related to the deal from Monaco.

When the problem with his medical cropped up, it prompted Everton to pursue a loan deal for Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee, who was happy to sign but was not allowed to leave Old Trafford. A move was also made for Aston Villa's Tammy Abraham but did not progress as the striker wished to remain at Villa Park.

After failing to sign an alternative, a deal was eventually agreed with Monaco, minutes before the deadline, which would have resulted in a smaller up-front payment and a series of triggered payments based on how he progressed. The player's personal terms were unchanged.

It was only then that the former Arsenal striker had his change of heart, leaving Finch Farm with Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro telling journalists at a news conference on Wednesday that Balogun was "not comfortable" with how Everton treated him during his medical.

Everton believe they supported Balogun throughout the process, while being open about the issues identified. The club also made clear to the player they would work with Monaco to explore a solution that could still enable the transfer to be completed.

To make matters worse, and to shed an even more unflattering light on the club's strategy and operation, it all came after hours after Everton had sanctioned striker Beto's £15.5m move to Fiorentina.

Events unfolded as Everton's most creative player Iliman Ndiaye was completing his £65m move to Manchester City.

Everton could point to the fact Balogun took a personal decision they could not reverse, but the bigger question is why they took until the final day of the window to address glaring long-term issues?

Kinnear, in what must now be looked upon as an ill-fated recent interview with BBC Radio Merseyside, announced Everton's squad was "in a good place", adding: "The challenge is we want to get the absolute best player we can in their position. Our metric is that by the close of the transfer window we have achieved that."

He also relayed the views of Everton's American owners that they regarded missing out on Europe last season as "failure". It was an announcement manager David Moyes admitted came as a "surprise".

After the events of recent days, the word "failure" is being applied to the owners and chief executive, not Moyes. And there will be no hiding place for TFG and Kinnear should things now go wrong.

The "good place" Kinnear spoke about has eventually amounted to leaving Moyes with just one striker in the raw Thierno Barry and only 18 senior, outfield players, a parlous state of affairs for the 63-year-old Scot, who has at times found it hard to disguise his dissatisfaction with the extent of the summer's transfer business.

Everton may have re-signed Jack Grealish on loan, and finally solved a right-back problem stretching back years by signing Ashley Maitland-Niles from Lyon for £3m, but the over-riding verdict on the club's transfer window has to be one of huge embarrassment for TFG and Kinnear.

Even the search for a right-back, a problem from last summer and further back, was not smooth, with Maitland-Niles being officially announced shortly after midnight after a £9.4m deal for Fulham's Kenny Tete was shelved when the Cottagers could not find a suitable replacement.

As well as only one striker in Barry, Everton's squad now has just one recognised right-back in Maitland-Niles and one left-back in Vitaliy Mykolenko after youngster Adam Aznou was allowed to join Malaga on loan.

The last few days have seen one major PR catastrophe narrowly avoided by pulling out of the sale of 19-year-old Armstrong, arguably Everton's most promising academy product since Wayne Rooney, only to walk straight into another, highly damaging one.

After the Carabao Cup second-round win at Preston North End, Moyes said: "I still think we have got a lot of work to do. We need more players. Our squad is not big enough and we need to get more quality in some areas if we can do."

Moyes' thoughts will be worth much more than a penny, should he choose to air them publicly, while fans' groups have wasted no time in expressing their undisguised anger, with a petition even set up calling for Kinnear's resignation.

"The Everton Fans' Forum" issued a lengthy statement featuring widescale criticism of the club, saying the Toffees' squad had been left "dangerously short" in key areas.

It added: "The conclusion of this summer's transfer window leaves Everton supporters with serious questions about the club's planning, recruitment and decision-making.

"This is not about demanding that Everton spend recklessly. Supporters understand the financial restrictions the club operates under. We are not demanding marquee signings simply for the sake of it.

"We are demanding competence, preparation and accountability."

And the influential group "The 1878s", volunteers who have created huge flags, banners and tifos to enhance the atmosphere at Everton's new Hill Dickinson Stadium, and whose efforts were described as "unbelievable" by Moyes, has responded to deadline day in similar vein.

In a statement it said it is "standing down for the foreseeable future" in protest, saying: "Like the rest of our fanbase, we are utterly disappointed and disgusted with how this transfer window has gone, especially the end of it.

"Also for fans asking, just to reiterate - when we design flags, there are rules and regulations that we have to adhere to regarding the wording on our flags during displays, we are not allowed derogatory or offensive wording or images.

"If we were able to get a load of flags in the ground to show our feelings of discontent, disappointment and anger over this whole situation, believe us, we would, but this is something that simply wouldn't be allowed."

As well as the last-day signings of Grealish and Maitland-Niles, Everton did make other acquisitions during the window, bringing in PFA Championship Player of the Year Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough.

Christian Norgaard was signed from Arsenal - although the 32-year-old Dane is currently injured with no comeback date - as a replacement for departed veteran Idrissa Gueye.

Deals for young German Merlin Rohl and England Under-21 winger Tyrique George, on loan last season, were confirmed. Brennan Johnson arrived from Crystal Palace in a straight swap with Dwight McNeil.

All this, however, has been overshadowed by a transfer deadline day that ended as nothing short of a debacle. In reality, they have ended this transfer markedly weaker than when they started it.

Everton are yet to issue any public statement on the events that have led to such damning criticism, fan rebellion and a loss of credibility for owners TFG - but there are many fences to be mended.

If that can be done successfully remains to be seen.

articles.title: White Sox’s John Schriffen has unfortunate gaffe while saying ‘retired’ during broadcast
articles.summary: Chicago White Sox announcer John Schriffen made a regrettable error on Tuesday night while calling a routine play between the Sox and Houston Astros. As Jose...
articles.body:
Chicago White Sox announcer John Schriffen made a regrettable error on Tuesday night while calling a routine play between the Sox and Houston Astros.

As Jose Altuve popped out to center field, Schriffen was on the call. While he meant to say that Altuve had been "retired," he instead used an outdated word for people with intellectual disabilities. He immediately caught and corrected himself to say "retired," but not in time to get his original misspeak back into his mouth.

Listening in real time, it's pretty clear that it was a simple accident on Schriffen's part, but it's an unfortunate slip of the tongue nonetheless. Unsurprisingly, the clip immediately made the rounds on social media, shared with varying levels of immaturity.

It's far from the first time an announcer has had such a moment in the booth. Chip Carey suffered a similar blunder last year while calling a game between the Cincinnati Reds and St. Louis Cardinals, and Baltimore Orioles announcer Gary Thorne made the exact same mistake as Schriffen did back in 2015 , with Albert Pujols taking the spot of Altuve.

It is not a good look to have this sort of slip, but it's also demonstrably better than some of the hot-mic moments we've heard from announcers who didn't realize their words were still going out to viewers at home .

Schriffen didn't address the comment afterward, and given how quickly he caught his error in the moment, he probably didn't need to. Mistakes happen, even if some sound way worse than others.

articles.title: Tiger Woods Returns To Court To Enter Stunning Plea
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is preparing to change his not guilty plea in the Florida DUI case stemming from his March rollover crash, marking a significant turn in a case t...
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is preparing to change his not guilty plea in the Florida DUI case stemming from his March rollover crash, marking a significant turn in a case that has kept the 15-time major champion in court for months.

Woods, 50, originally pleaded not guilty to two misdemeanor charges on March 31. Court records now show that he is scheduled to appear Wednesday for a change-of-plea hearing. Whether that change comes as part of an agreement with prosecutors remains unclear.

The charges include property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test.

According to police , Woods was driving at high speed along a beachside road in Jupiter Island, Florida, when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer and rolled onto its side. Authorities estimated the damage to the other vehicle at roughly $5,000.

Woods escaped the Land Rover without suffering injuries. He later told officers that he had been looking at his phone and changing the radio around the time of the collision.

Police Say Opioids Were Found After the Crash

A Breathalyzer test detected no alcohol in his system. Police said Woods refused to provide a urine sample; however, deputies reported finding two opioid tablets in his pocket. The sheriff's report also stated that Woods displayed signs of impairment.

The investigation later expanded to include Woods' medical and prescription records.

In July, Martin County Circuit Court Judge Darren Steele approved an agreement allowing prosecutors to request hospital records associated with Woods' treatment following the crash. Steele had previously approved a similar arrangement in May that gave prosecutors access to prescription medication records from Woods' Palm Beach pharmacy covering the period from January 1 through the March collision.

Those records are subject to a protective order restricting their release to prosecutors, law enforcement, state experts and Woods' defense team.

The case has unfolded while Woods has remained largely removed from competitive golf. Before the March crash, he had reportedly been moving toward another comeback and was widely expected to compete at the Masters.

Woods has not played competitively since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon. Since then, he has undergone surgery for a torn Achilles as well as a seventh procedure on his back.

The March collision also added another chapter to Woods' long history of highly publicized incidents behind the wheel.

In February 2021, Woods suffered serious injuries when the SUV he was driving left the road in California and rolled down an embankment. The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said he was traveling at approximately 80 mph in an area where the speed limit was substantially lower. He was not charged with driving under the influence in that case.

Four years earlier, Woods encountered police near his Florida home under very different circumstances.

In May 2017, Jupiter police found him unconscious behind the wheel of his Mercedes-Benz at approximately 3 a.m. Officers found the vehicle stopped awkwardly along the roadside, with signs of damage.

Once again, alcohol was not detected. Toxicology testing instead found several substances, including the active ingredient in marijuana, the painkillers Vicodin and Dilaudid, the sleep medication Ambien and the anti-anxiety medication Xanax.

Woods said afterward that he had experienced an unexpected reaction to prescription medications while attempting to manage pain and insomnia following back surgery.

He ultimately pleaded guilty to reckless driving. His sentence included one year of probation, a $250 fine, and 50 hours of community service. He was also prohibited from drinking alcohol during his probation.

That summer, Woods announced that he had completed a private treatment program dealing with his use of pain medication.

"I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends," Woods wrote at the time. "I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received."

From the 2009 Crash to a New Florida Court Date

But the driving incident that became inseparable from Woods' public downfall occurred years earlier.

In November 2009, Woods crashed his Cadillac Escalade near his Florida home, striking a fire hydrant, a tree, and several hedges. He suffered minor injuries and received a citation for careless driving.

The crash happened just days after the National Enquirer published allegations linking Woods romantically to New York nightclub manager Rachel Uchitel. What initially appeared to be a relatively minor single-vehicle accident quickly became part of the intense scrutiny surrounding Woods' personal life and marriage to Elin Nordegren.

Now, nearly 17 years after that episode, Woods is again heading into a Florida courtroom because of an incident behind the wheel.

This time, however, prosecutors have obtained medical and prescription information connected to the case, and Woods' decision to change his original not guilty plea suggests Wednesday's hearing could substantially alter the course of the proceedings. Exactly what plea Woods intends to enter, and whether prosecutors have agreed to any concessions in return, has yet to be disclosed.

articles.title: Browns face growing heat over Deshaun Watson call as Shedeur Sanders uproar explodes
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns backed quarterback Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders, but critics warn his leash may already be dangerously short.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson opens the season atop Cleveland's depth chart, but the runway under him looks unusually thin. The Browns kept him as their Week 1 starter against the Jacksonville Jaguars and passed on handing the job to rookie Shedeur Sanders, a decision that has already drawn criticism.

Watson's track record in Cleveland gives them reason for caution. Across his time with the franchise since 2022, he has connected on 61.2% of his throws for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions.

Former receiver Chad Johnson laid out the math that could force a change. Speaking to OutKick, he pointed to a schedule that starts with Jacksonville, rolls into Tampa Bay, then returns home, and argued the Browns cannot afford to fall into an early hole.

"If you start off 0-2, they're making a move," Johnson said , adding the team would act "before the season gets too far away from them." He framed Watson's grip on the role as fragile from the start. "Deshaun Watson was always going to be the starting quarterback no matter what," Johnson said, before warning that "his leash is going to be very short."

Head coach Todd Monken defended the choice on his own terms. He credited Watson's "whole body of work over the course of offseason" and pushed back on the idea that the job would be a "week-to-week" question.

Skip Bayless Blasts Browns Over Shedeur Sanders' Blocked Path

Sanders' situation has become the season's loudest sideshow, and Skip Bayless is leading the outrage. The commentator called what the Browns are doing to Sanders one of the worst setups he has watched, saying on X on August 31, 2026, that it is "THE most outrageously wrong situation I've ever seen."

The frustration builds on a summer that never broke Sanders' way. He came into 2026 fighting for the starting job before the team settled on Watson, leaving him in a backup role after a rookie year that, by most accounts, showed real growth.

A later decision stung more. Cleveland had Sanders split scout-team snaps with rookie Taylen Green rather than funnel every extra developmental rep his way.

An opening looked possible when Dillon Gabriel landed on injured reserve with a back injury. It did not translate into a bigger share of work behind Watson for Sanders .

The pushback has not come only from Bayless. Robert Griffin III reported that Watson was not Monken's pick, and that many inside the building saw Sanders as the better fit on and off the field, with the team wanting Watson to "play for his pay." For now, Sanders waits.

articles.title: ‘It’s part of the game’ – Thiago Scuro explains Lamine Camara’s failed Chelsea move and Folarin Balogun’s decision to reject Everton
articles.summary: AS Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro held a press conference, attended by Get French Football News, in La Turbie on Wednesday afternoon to explain how Lamine Camara’s...
articles.body:
AS Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro held a press conference, attended by Get French Football News, in La Turbie on Wednesday afternoon to explain how Lamine Camara's (22) move to Chelsea and Folarin Balogun's (25) move to Everton broke down during the final hours of transfer deadline day. The Principality club's CEO notably denied that Monaco were "the bad guys" in the room regarding Camara's failed move, and also revealed that it is Balogun who opted against Everton after Everton's medical staff diagnosed a problem that, according to his personal medical staff, made "no sense at all".

Thiago, can you explain what happened last night? There were two deals that were on, off, back on again, and ultimately off….

I think that is a good place to start to speak not just about the last two days but the last 10 days. I've been saying that our strategy this summer is very clear. We need to generate money, as we've been saying, pushed by regulations and by everything that we've been discussing over the last few years in terms of financial constraints in our league. We had a clear plan to talk about the two topics. We also made clear that our priority was to keep Lamine in the club. It's going to be his third season; normally, it's the cycle that we do. We try to protect also the performance, because the performance is strongly connected to the financial situation of the club as well.

Clearly, we were open to discussing and finding a transfer for Balogun. He finished his third season. We had already worked in advance to replace him, and we were fully ready to do this. Things went very well with this strategy until we were almost there. Basically, to talk about Lamine, we'd been approached by several clubs during the summer. The message has always been the same: our priority is that he stays, even yesterday morning after the training session. We had a conversation with Lamine directly, which was very okay and friendly, where he also showed the desire to stay, that he was happy in the club.

During the day, we had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton. Balogun flew yesterday morning to go for medicals and sign a contract. Our plan worked very well in this moment in terms of revenue generation, squad planning, player transfers. Thilo (Kehrer) going, as announced, opened the space in the salary that we needed with the DNCG (French football's financial watchdog). Balogun, besides the salary, was also an important source of income for the club, which would help us also to balance the season. And then, Lamine staying.

This was what we had until mid-afternoon. What happened is that Chelsea was always testing and trying. What about Lamine? What about Lamine? I've been talking to them for the last 10 days. Around 4 p.m. yesterday, we got a contact from Chelsea. Okay, we sold a player in this position (Enzo Fernandez). Deal done. Is there any possibility that Monaco is open to selling Lamine? The answer was the same. No, it's not. At this moment, at 4 p.m, Balogun was in Liverpool undergoing his medical. Everything was going pretty well. Around 7 p.m., we were contacted by Everton, raising questions about Balogun's medical, which, for our medical staff, as well as for the player's personal medical staff, made no sense at all.

The explanations were not enough to justify or to bring concerns regarding the future of the player, which there aren't. This discussion started between medical departments from here and there. It took Everton around 2-3 hours to go deep into the assessment and check with other doctors. This is a normal situation when the doctor of the club raises concerns. It's quite normal that clubs will look for other specialists, share the images and discuss the case. This was ongoing.

Scuro on Camara's failed move to Chelsea: 'It is part of the game'

Meanwhile, as with everything in the last days, this was in the press quite quickly. I would say around half an hour after we were contacted. It was already in the media that Balogun has failed his medical. And then, of course, Chelsea saw the opportunity. 'OK, Monaco needs money. Balogun is struggling there. Let's go. Let's try.' And this is the game. It's fair to play this game. There is no problem. Chelsea came and called us. Oh, maybe I can be here for the solution. And at that moment, we had to open the door for the discussion.

This was almost 8 p.m. We started negotiations with Chelsea. I informed the player directly myself. I called him. I informed his agent, as we always do. Very open. We had discussions about the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea. At the same time, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balogun. And what happened was that around 10 p.m, in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that, OK, there is no problem. We are ready to do it. Let's sign the contract. As soon as we got the information, we came back to Chelsea and thought, OK, we have our deal there. There is no deal on it. Because it's also fair to do this. It's also part of the game. There is no reason that these kinds of discussions are dynamic on the last day of the transfer window, which all of us decided to be on the last day, trying to find solutions, with the clock ticking, that now this kind of interaction [sees us] become the bad guys in the room. That Monaco is 'not fair, Monaco is not right. Everybody is very fair and nice in the football industry. Just Monaco is not.' Too much.

Balogun 'not comfortable' about making Everton move after doubts raised in medical

So this is the storytelling. We informed, again, everyone that there was no deal with Chelsea. We progressed. The Premier League has a mechanism in which you can request one extra hour to finish the paperwork. This was done. Five minutes to close the transfer window there, for us to finish all the paperwork between Monaco and Everton and 'Balo'. I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract. At the last moment, the players decided not to sign. And basically, Balogun's allegation is that I'm not feeling well because of the way the club treated me. I'm not feeling well because Everton's medical department raised doubts about my future or my health. I have nothing (no health problem), so I'm not comfortable signing a long contract here. And that's the way we finish our transfer window.

So basically, the story about those two players and what happened yesterday was also new for me. It's the first time in my career that I saw a last day (deadline day) like this. It's not nice to stay the last two days of the transfer window until 3 a.m. in the office, trying to find solutions here and there. And this is something that we need to try to do better as a club, because it puts everyone in a situation where what is happening can happen. And it's not nice to be here, having to explain and having to face all the consequences of this. And the reality is now that we are very, very happy that Lamine stayed. We want to be strong on the pitch. We want to grow this season, and we are going for that. And now we are still waiting for 'Balo' to come back for us to sit and discuss and to realise between us what's next. We still have other markets open, which we are having discussions about with different players, including 'Balo'. Let's see what can still happen until Thursday, because we still have markets that have the financial capacity to do something. And this is what happened, and this is where we are today.

Have the promises to the DNCG as it pertains to the wage bill been kept?

Not completely, no, because 'Balo' leaving was the trigger to get everything OK. Our financial plan was working almost perfectly until 7 p.m. Salary reduction was on target. We were able to bring the players that we want. We had everything approved by the DNCG in advance. We would have a very small financial gap to cover in the winter. Everything was very, very well done. Unfortunately, the facts that I mentioned before happened, and now we have to face this situation and find solutions in different ways. And we are already working on that.

Can Balogun stay and do you blame him for not signing for Everton?

Today, he is a Monaco player. There is a chance that he stays. On Everton, I was not there. We have to respect his decision. We tried to do the work on the club side. We found solutions. Even in slightly better conditions for the player and for Monaco in terms of payment flow. And the reality is that when 'Balou 'Balo' mentioned to us this feeling that he was not comfortable, he didn't want to sign. We didn't see ourselves in a position to push him. We had to respect.

Do you think that Everton tried to play a game with Monaco?

My intention here, as always, is to work and protect AS Monaco. I don't want to create a war with Chelsea. I don't want to create a war with Everton. It's not my role to be here judging whatever anyone did at other clubs. Every time I need to create a conflict or creating a decision to protect AS Monaco, I will do it. This is what I've been doing since I'm here. It's for the organisation. It's not for myself. It's not to be loved by people outside. It's not to be loved by other clubs. It's to give AS Monaco what AS Monaco needs. And this is what we did yesterday.

For Balogun, I only spoke to him by phone. His arguments are clear. He's coming back. I think he took the decision. There is not a big reason for him to be affected too much because it's his decision. On Lamine, I really respect and understand. Because the player might have got excited yesterday during the day by conversations with the coach. By everything that a club like Chelsea can propose and promise to a player. At the end of the day, he also asked us to try to find a solution for him to leave. But again, we explained the reasons why we did what we did. And now we're going to keep respecting and working with him. Knowing his mentality and hischaracter, we can expect him full power in the next game. And he's going to keep building his career.

As with many other players, better things will come in the future. This is not the end of the world. It's just one possibility for a player on his level with his talent. I'm very confident that soon he will have even better options and offers than the one he had yesterday.

Do you have any regrets? In hindsight, would you have done things differently?

First of all, we should try and discuss whether it makes sense that our transfer window closes before the Premier League because this causes a lot of problems.This was part of my discussion during the afternoon with Chelsea. We closed at 8 p.m. I don't have the time to stay until 1 a.m signing players.

So to protect French clubs, maybe we are becoming more than ever a selling league. Maybe we should start discussing following other countries that stay one day more, two days more. Like Belgium is doing, like Turkey is doing and other markets, because it's a way to protect the local clubs. So this is the first point. And the second, well, I'm not a guy of regretting anything. Every time you look back on things already done, all of us may do something different here and there. Because we already know the outcome.

Of course, if I knew that at 1 a.m Balogun would not sign the contract, would I do something different before? Of course. But with the elements we had, with the information we had, in my view, we made very good decisions. Unfortunately, the outcome is not the one we expected.

I don't think so. I think what happened is that, yes, we had other offers. At the end of the day, Balogun decided to go to Everton. This also made me a bit sad yesterdaywhen the topic of the medicals came up because the player refused other things to go there. And again, we are judging facts. After the fact, it's always easier. But I don't think we were setting very high expectations because we never give a price. We are open to listening to offers. And from there, we discuss. This is the way we work. We don't work like this. We are open. We listen to the offer and from there, we progress. I think the whole industry somehow uses the market value of theplayers as a reference. The market value of Balogun today is €50m on Transfermarkt , for example.

Did this prevent you from recruiting other players? There was talk of Erik Lira and Fares Ghedjemis arriving…

Yes, this is a good point. On this, we were also very sad yesterday. The situation with Erik Lira, our relationship with Cruz Azul… I want to really thank them, and I appreciate the way they dealt with everything with us. The deal was ready. The player was ready to travel. Everything was absolutely pressing on the button. But it wasmandatory in the agreement that Balogun would open the foreign (Non-EU) spot; because of that, we were not able to bring Erik Lira. That was our desire.Having to call the player and say, I'm sorry, we couldn't make it. As a human, it's a very hard part of the job, on the transfer window. Could he join in January? It depends on several things. We are not in a position to ask them to wait, keep holding. But for sure, it's a player that has our attention and respect.

Could Camara be offerred a contract extension? And also, by how much did you have to reduce the wage bill this summer?

We had to reduce our wage bill by almost 20% from last season. At the moment, we still need to find solutions and discuss with the DNCG how to manage it. We are doing that in a transparent way. Regarding Lamine, it can be an option if his intention is to stay longer at the club. It is something to be discussed. He still has three years remaining.

It is possible. It depends on what happens with players leaving, creating space in the wage bill. It is a possibility that Monaco can have a 'joker' during this first half of the season. Yes, it can happen. Only in the event of a departure? Exactly.

GFFN | Luke Entwistle – reporting from Monaco

articles.title: Iowa football set to start 'impressive' transfer DB Anthony Hawkins
articles.summary: Longtime Iowa head football coach Kirk Ferentz had great things to say about the Hawkeyes' starting strong safety, Anthony Hawkins.
articles.body:
Iowa 's safety position will look different this season. Xavier Nwankpa went on to the NFL, where he has found a home with the Kansas City Chiefs . His starting safety partner, Koen Entringer, transferred to Louisville not long after.

With a pair of talented defensive backs departing the program, Kirk Ferentz knew he had to hit the transfer portal to fill that roster hole.

Ferentz and the Hawkeyes did exactly that, bringing in a trio of transfer safeties: third-year Tyler Brown from James Madison, third-year Xavier Styles from Robert Morris and third-year Anthony Hawkins from Villanova. Brown was the most highly regarded of the group, with many expecting him to start right away on the back end.

However, an offseason injury has put a wrench in those plans.

Brown is still nursing a muscle strain and didn't appear on Iowa's season-opening depth chart . In his absence, Ferentz named Hawkins as the starter at strong safety. In his media availability on Tuesday, the longtime head coach broke down what's stood out to him about Hawkins' game this offseason.

"He's been impressive," Ferentz said. "He's an impressive young guy and did a good job last year at his previous stop, and we were intrigued when he showed up here in January. He's been good every phase of the way. Still learning, still growing. There's a lot to learn back there, especially at the safety position. There's a lot of thought process and what have you. It helps he's got a guy like (Zach) Lutmer back there helping him. No, he's done a really good job, and he does have good range. He's a big, tall guy. Probably one of the taller safeties I've ever seen, at least since we've been here. Eager to see him play. He's done a good job in practice."

Hawkins, a 6-foot-3 safety from Annapolis, Md., was stellar with Villanova in 2025. He racked up 57 total tackles, nine passes defended, two interceptions, and a forced fumble en route to being named an FCS Freshman All-American. He brings a big frame and a knack for being around the football, a great trait for a defensive back to have.

The Hawkeyes will rely on Hawkins to step up with Brown sidelined. When the latter returns to the mix, Iowa could have one of the better, under-the-radar defensive back rooms in the Big Ten.
