articles.title: Mike Trout speaks candidly about 'needed' sale of Angels
articles.summary: The Angels' longtime star shared his thoughts on the team's sale on Tuesday.
articles.body:
There aren't many — if any — figures across baseball who are more equipped to speak publicly about the state of the Los Angeles Angels than Mike Trout.

Over the past 16 years, Trout hasn't just become a future Hall of Fame player in an Angels uniform. He's repeatedly voiced his commitment to the franchise through plenty of struggles, making just one postseason appearance in his illustrious career.

Significant change is coming for the Angels, though, with Tuesday's reported sale of $4 billion to Stan Kroenke.

Here's what Trout had to say about the Angels' sale.

Mike Trout speaks on Angels sale to Stan Kroenke

For years, Angels fans and figures across baseball have criticized Arte Moreno as one of the worst owners in baseball. Moreno, who bought the team in 2003 during an era of success, has slowly let the franchise fall out of annual contention between disastrous free-agent contracts (Albert Pujols, Anthony Rendon), an unwillingness to rebuild and a failure to reach the postseason with Trout and Shohei Ohtani , two all-time players.

With Moreno making the decision to sell, though, there's a sense of renewed hope in Anaheim — and Trout seems to be on board with it.

"I'm excited," Trout said Tuesday of the sale, per ESPN . "Look, the track record -- it's there."

Kroenke is the controlling owner of a collection of successful sports franchises, including the NFL's Rams, NBA's Nuggets and Premier League's Arsenal F.C. He's often been praised for both his financial commitments to his teams and his willingness to take a step back, allowing front offices to make decisions.

"Seeing the reaction from the fans and some of the guys and the whole vibe, I think it was needed for a fresh start," Trout said, per ESPN. "The biggest thing is getting that feeling of getting that winning culture back and having that vibe in the clubhouse."

Trout and Angels shortstop Zach Neto also said they reached out to Rams players Tuesday to get a feel for Kroenke, told the new Angels owner "just wants what's important for us" and "will invest in anything they need behind the scenes."

"It's obviously been frustrating the last, I don't know how many years it's been," Trout said, per ESPN. "But just to hear the news like this, I'm super excited to have this change."

One of the most pressing immediate questions following the Angels sale — and one that has stuck with the franchise for years — was whether Trout will be sticking around. He's under contract through 2030, and the star outfielder made it clear he plans to continue playing in Anaheim, saying the sale "doesn't change" his desire to stay with the franchise for the remainder of his contract.

Trout is playing on the 12-year, $426.5 million extension he signed with the Angels in 2019, with 2026 marking the eighth year of the contract. As he approaches his late 30s, still an All-Star outfielder, he'll be carrying an annual salary of $37.12 million, per Spotrac.

Trout isn't set to hit free agency until the winter after his age-38 season in 2030.

articles.title: Highest-spending clubs of the transfer window: Man City, Chelsea and more lead team rankings
articles.summary: The Premier League once again led the way in European soccer with a gargantuan summer 2026 window.
articles.body:
The summer transfer window reached a frantic conclusion on Tuesday, September 1, with the Premier League once again the fulcrum of multi-million-dollar spending.

Manchester City dropped in excess of $250 million on deadline day alone to bring in Illiman Ndiaye (pictured) and Enzo Fernandez from Everton and Chelsea , respectively.

Fernandez and his new teammate Elliot Anderson join the small but growing ranks of men with price tags in excess of £100m in the Premier League. At Liverpool , Bradley Barcola joins Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz in England's most expensively assembled attacking trio of all time.

Barcola left two-time reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain, who, along with Clasico giants Barcelona and Real Madrid , have been more circumspect this time around.

Which team spent the most in this transfer window?

Man City's deadline-day splurge puts them at the top of the spending charts for summer 2026, giving Enzo Maresca an impressively tooled squad as he seeks to build upon Pep Guardiola's remarkable legacy at the Etihad Stadium.

Chelsea are the next biggest spenders, although the Fernandez sale and the collapse of a deal for intended replacement Lamine Camara from Monaco mean they ended up with positive net spend.

Tottenham Hotspur have embarked upon a hasty and expensive rebuild, yet to yield a Premier League point or a goal, while Newcastle United and Aston Villa have each seen plenty of business in and out.

Madrid and Barcelona are the only non-Premier League teams in the top 10, sandwiching newly promoted Ipswich Town .

Highest-spending clubs of the transfer window

Most money spent in a single transfer window

The Premier League once again set a new record for spending in a summer transfer window with a total $4.76 billion outlay, breaking the previous record of $4.17bn set 12 months ago. Prior to summer 2025, the Premier League had not exceeded $3.25bn in a summer window.

Italy's Serie A has spent over $1bn collectively in each of the past five years, but never up to $1.5bn. Ligue 1 is the only other division to surpass $1bn during this period, thanks almost entirely to Paris Saint-Germain's summer 2023 spending.

La Liga's spending, despite the power of Madrid and Barcelona, has been less than that of other rival leagues after Spain's soccer authorities brought in strict financial regulations.

Big 5 leagues recent summer transfer spending

Clubs with lowest net spend in this transfer window

Paris Saint-Germain have frequently topped the spending charts, but a settled squad and the sale of Barcola this summer meant they top Europe's net-spend table.

Luis Enrique's club have spent $176m to bring in the likes of Maghnes Akliouche and Ferran Torres, but Barcola's switch to Anfield and Goncalo Ramos and Ibrahim Mbaye's moves to AC Milan and Aston Villa respectively have contributed to a positive transfer balance of $211.1m.

PSG are one of three Ligue 1 clubs to have a transfer balance in excess of £100m this summer. Lille brought in big money for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, while Strasbourg's $46.3m sale of Valentin Barco to affiliated club Chelsea helped them to a healthy balance sheet.

West Ham have absorbed relegation from the Premier League, and selling the likes of Mateus Fernandes has left them in a decent financial position.

articles.title: ‘I Disagree With It’ – Titans Called Out by Jared Stillman Over Pulling Media Credentials After Cam Ward Incident
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans found themselves under heavy criticism after revoking the media credentials of reporter and podcaster Jared Stillman. This move came aft...
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans found themselves under heavy criticism after revoking the media credentials of reporter and podcaster Jared Stillman. This move came after Stillman had a rather unpleasant exchange with franchise quarterback Cam Ward last week.

On Tuesday, Stillman posted on X to confirm that the Tennessee Titans called and banned him, backing up Titans beat reporter Paul Kuharsky's original report. Stillman, on his podcast "Stillman & Co." said

"So, the news is out today. I got a call from the Tennessee Titans, and I believe it was a professional call, but it was an uncomfortable call nonetheless."

He claimed the franchise argued that as a YouTuber, he doesn't need the same locker-room access as daily beat reporters.

"Their logic was what I do as a YouTuber does not require media access from the team," he said. "I'm not a daily beat writer and I'm not on local radio anymore."

The Titans maintained that the ban was due to his overall reporting style, rather than just his viral clash with Cam Ward this week.

"The Titans told me that this wasn't about one singular instance, though I think a lot of people are going to assume that it's about what happened on Thursday with Cam Ward," Stillman said.

Jared Stillman's Argument With Titans QB Cam Ward

Vols reporter Ryan Schumpert supported Stillman, slammed the decision as embarrassing, and called the Titans organization "soft."

"Shameful move. What a soft franchise," he wrote on X.

Kuharsky, who broke the story, expressed his take on the team's heavy-handed decision:

"Stillman's style and methods make him an easy test case," Kuharsky wrote . "That's also what makes this worth watching. A credentialing standard matters most when it's applied to someone whose coverage or conduct a team doesn't like. Without the Titans explaining what standard Stillman violated, it's impossible to know whether this was enforcement of a legitimate credentialing policy or punishment of an irritating critic."

This media storm erupted right after Stillman's recent argument with quarterback Cam Ward. Last week, Stillman pressed Ward to grade his own play during the preseason. Ward shut him down immediately

"I'm glad you don't think so," Ward said. "That's good."

Losing his press pass means Stillman's show will lack direct, on-the-record reactions from the team. The Titans organization has yet to release an official statement on the matter.

Is this a fair policy or just a franchise silencing an annoying critic? Only time will shed more light on it.
